Record the step in its state candidate, extracted The step, the declaration that named it, its state, what was seen, and — for anything not done — exactly what to do next. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_RecordStep . Record the verdict on the node candidate, extracted Findings are advice, not commits — the same separation the generic reviewer lane keeps. Record them where the next reader meets the node. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/review-code.bpmn#Task_RecordVerdict . Record what did not classify cleanly candidate, extracted Factors that sit in two quadrants, or in none, are written down as such. The source states this as inherent rather than as analyst error: "the same factor can be fitted in two categories. A factor can be a strength and a weakness at the same time." It adds the two drifts — strengths not maintained become weaknesses, and opportunities not taken but taken by competitors become threats. A scan that silently forced every factor into one quadrant would report a cleanliness the method does not have. This is the same third-state discipline the rest of this repository applies to "could not determine": an unclassifiable factor is a finding, not a blank. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_RecordAmbiguous . Record what failed candidate, extracted Which check failed, on which items, and the evidence. The landed copy is not removed: a failed import is information about the source or the store, and deleting the copy would destroy the evidence. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/sample-import.bpmn#Task_RecordFindings . Record what is still open candidate, extracted outcome: unsettled with what was asked and what is still open, so the next actor resumes rather than restarts. An agent that reaches for a default here has produced a guess, not a determination. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_RecordUnsettled . Record what is still open candidate, extracted Declined, or silent where no default is allowed. The record says what was asked and what is still open, so the next actor resumes rather than restarts. Never a guess. When it is the context, the Role or the Process that is still open, say so and stop: a step completed in the wrong Process records an authority that was never given. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_RecordUnsettled . Record what this is a copy of candidate, extracted The step that is easy to omit and impossible to reconstruct afterwards. provenance is a PAIR: upstream is the remote thing, local is the original in this repository. A copy-out writes local; it does not overwrite upstream, and it does not reuse upstream for a local value. Without local, one rename later the copy is indistinguishable from original work and nothing downstream can repair it, because the information was never written down. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/copy-out-materialized.bpmn#Task_RecordProvenance . Record why it is not a substrate; write no entry candidate, extracted No subscription entry is written for a repository that is not a substrate. What is recorded is the reason (non-conforming, no harness, or unreachable) and the pin it was asked at, so a later attempt at a different commit starts from what failed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Refuse . Record x,y for this note on THIS board candidate, extracted Record the note's x,y in the layout layer for THIS board, naming the note by id. An existing card dragged here only gets a new position — placing is not creating, so no content is duplicated. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-place-note.bpmn#A_Place . Refresh updatedAt only candidate, extracted Nothing changed, and saying so is the point. A record that stops being written looks exactly like an abandoned session; a refreshed timestamp with no other change says the session is alive and idle, which is a different fact and the commonest one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/session-state-machine.bpmn#A_Touch . Refresh materialized content candidate, extracted Refresh is not re-import: what changed upstream, what changed locally since, and what to do when both did. The shared subprocess answers all three, and re-asks the five gates, since a licence can change and a collection can grow past the size agreed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/sample-import.bpmn#Call_Refresh . Refresh the held part candidate, extracted The shared refresh, called, not re-described: what changed upstream, what changed locally, and what to do when both did. An archival copy is fixity-checked and never re-fetched. Whatever that process decides — refreshed, kept divergent, or deferred — is the part's new state; this loop only moves to the next part. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Call_Refresh . Refresh the templates candidate, extracted Re-run the layer's extractors, once for every locale: pages, diagrams, glossary schemes. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_Templates . Refuse: no flow for this source kind candidate, extracted A kind added to the union (a graph database, say) before this diagram and the mount tool learn it. Refused with its own exit code — reading it as a directory would scan an empty path and report it clean. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_RefuseUnknownKind . Rehearse self-contained candidate, extracted bun run cat seed:ready --layer <name> --rehearse copies the layer and what it needs into a scratch workspace of sibling directories and runs the tests there. Run the gates rather than scanning imports: a static scan misses files the gates load at run time, and renaming the directory changes every generated page. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Rehearse . Rehearse standalone candidate, extracted Copy the content and the tools alone into a temporary directory, with nothing else on the path, and run the tools' checks there. An empty tree must exit non-zero, so a rehearsal over nothing cannot pass. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-prepare.bpmn#Task_Rehearse . Related work: find, sort, ask candidate, extracted When the requirement is initiated or updated through a human-agent chat, search the beans and the repository's issues and open PRs for relevance, categorize and summarize them, and ask the user whether and how to coordinate. Judgement decides the categories; the user decides the coordination. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-issue-linking.bpmn#Call_RelatedWork . Related work: find, sort, ask candidate, extracted Search beans, issues and open PRs for work the method touches, categorize and summarize them, and ask the owner whether and how to coordinate. CRDM calls the same sub-process. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/methodology-from-source.bpmn#Call_RelatedWork . Relations and cardinalities, both ways candidate, extracted Stated in both directions, because "one attestation per report" and "one report per attestation" are different claims and a model with only the first cannot say whether a re-signature is an update or a second row. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#A_Relations . Relocate the content to the trashcan candidate, extracted Relocate the confirmed content — that one thing, not the class it belongs to — to the trashcan. The folio changes first, because the folio carries what is true. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_MoveContent . Remove the artefact candidate, extracted rm -rf branches/<slug>. Cannot reach the log, which lives outside branches/ — structural rather than guarded, because a branch named to collide with a directory under branches/ slugifies to exactly that name and git permits the ref. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/staging-render-log.bpmn#A_Remove . Render and push to GitHub Pages candidate, extracted BOUND BY THE TOOL, so no calledElement is written here: the gh-pages Tool lists the process this descends into, render-kg-to-github-pages, and that process is held by a layer cat-harness does not need, so naming it would bind upward. What it does: make sure gh-pages exists and Pages serves it, stage, check the staging, commit onto gh-pages, check what is served. It returns the status and the message Task_Report records. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/render-kg-to-cdn.bpmn#Call_GitHubPages . Render and push with that CDN's own Tool candidate, extracted BOUND BY THE TOOL, so no calledElement is written here, and only on this branch: the CDN is not GitHub Pages, and its Tool, which a higher layer owns (a Cloudflare publish, for one), lists the process this descends into. A lower layer cannot name a higher layer\'s process. Whatever the Tool, it returns the same status and message. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/render-kg-to-cdn.bpmn#Call_ToolSubprocess . Render every card as its avatar candidate, extracted Render every card as its avatar — the starting state. Each content kind controls its own avatar; the board decides only that nothing starts open. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-open-close.bpmn#A_RenderAvatars . Render the method: adopted vs refused candidate, extracted What the source says, section by section, then a table of what this platform adopts and what it refuses, each with a reason. Extensions beyond the source (such as web plus mobile where the paper studied mobile) are stated as ours. Reported results are not imported as facts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/methodology-from-source.bpmn#A_Render . Render them in the artifact's own pages candidate, extracted The statements are written into pages of the folio's working artifact, so a reader of the artifact finds them without leaving it. HOW the pages look is the content type's: its adapter renders them in its own format (pages of a document, a section of a paper, pages of an implementation guide), as its content profile declares. Each statement carries two links: to the library entry's page, and to the section, labelled as collected. The pages are GENERATED: a person edits the extraction or the source, never the page. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/publish-extracted-statements.bpmn#Task_RenderArtifact . Report every step candidate, extracted One report, every step in its state, with counts: done, not done, could not determine, stated — led by the primary step, the JSON Schemas and JSON-LD at their IRIs. Required, which is what drawing the call says: an initialization that finished with steps open must say which. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_Report . Report node-view coverage candidate, extracted The Tool node-view-coverage (bun run cat node-views:report -- --site <built site>) counts, per layer, folder and kind, which nodes have an IRI, a .jsonld, a page and a row on their folder page, and which folder links are dead or point at the raw repository. A QA report, not a gate: it always exits 0 and feeds no gateway, and its results go to test/results/node-views/ and on to the qa-reports branch. A graph with no viewer is still shown inert and labelled by the tile step; this says how many of its nodes are owed a page. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/harness-default-rendering.bpmn#A_NodeViews . Report source errors as one issue candidate, extracted Any source-text error the translators found goes into one issue on the source, with its location. When there is none, this step writes nothing. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_SourceIssue . Report the measurement; ship nothing candidate, extracted Write the measurement and what was tried into the work context, and ask the owner whether the slice should ship at that size, be cut further, or not exist. Nothing is wired: no manifest is published, no gate added, no deploy line written. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/slice-sqlite-publish.bpmn#A_Report . Report the push: status and message candidate, extracted pages-status.ts: pushed, not-pushed or could-not-determine, and one line — the commit, the root URL, and the QA of both the staging and what is served. On the path from a failed staging it says not-pushed and names the problem. Required on every path: a caller that gets no status cannot tell a push from nothing. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_Report . Report the push: status and message candidate, extracted The output, on every path: pushed, not-pushed or could-not-determine, and one message — what is live (a commit), at which root URL, and the QA result. From the no-Tool branch the status is not-pushed and the message names the target nobody implements. A check that could not look is never reported as pushed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/render-kg-to-cdn.bpmn#Task_Report . Report what moves — sizes, what breaks candidate, extracted The agent reports and waits: what would move, how large, what in the parent breaks, and the rollback. deletion-requires-confirmation is not a courtesy to waive: an agent never removes or relocates a durable artefact on its own initiative. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-authorise.bpmn#Task_Propose . Report what would move — sizes, and what breaks candidate, extracted The agent reports and waits: what would move, how large, what in the parent breaks, and the rollback. deletion-requires-confirmation is not a courtesy to waive: an agent never removes or relocates a durable artefact on its own initiative. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_ReportWhatMoves . Report what would move — sizes, and what breaks candidate, extracted The agent reports and waits: what would move, how large, what in the parent breaks, and the rollback. deletion-requires-confirmation is not a courtesy to waive: an agent never removes or relocates a durable artefact on its own initiative. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Propose . Request completion of remaining strings candidate, extracted Return to the translator with a list of untranslated or fuzzy strings that need attention. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_RequestMoreWork . Resolve each harness's page ground candidate, extracted The theme art for that harness's pages, all three crops or none, and the URL scopes that make a page that harness's (pageGround). The site owner's ground is the fallback for a page no scope claims. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/harness-default-rendering.bpmn#A_Ground . Resolve the closure at the pin candidate, extracted Fetch the pinned tree (shallow, blobless). Read the harness's declaration from it; for each needs name, find that layer in the same tree, else follow a GITLINK at that tree as a pin into its own repository. A need found in neither is missing; one the downstream already holds is local. Paths and directories come from mountDefaults unless overridden. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-dependency.bpmn#Task_ResolveClosure . Resolve the kind's zoom threshold candidate, extracted Resolve the semantic-zoom threshold for each card's kind: the folio default unless the kind overrides it with a stated because. Return the source alongside the value, so a card that flipped too early can be traced to a decision or to a default. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-open-close.bpmn#A_ResolveThreshold . Resolve the subgraph's content source candidate, extracted declaredSubgraph(start, id): the declaring layer, the entry, and the resolved source with declaredIn saying which layer answered. Never read source off the declaration directly — the config override and the legacy storage field are folded in by the resolver and nowhere else. A contradiction (both source and storage; a qa subgraph keyed by tip) throws here, before anything is mounted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_ResolveSource . Resolve the Subgraphs and the root URL candidate, extracted Read the instance's declaration. Every Subgraph id asked for must be one it declares; none asked for means the whole graph. The root URL is the one given, else the declaration's iriBase, else https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/. An unknown id is refused, never rendered as a smaller site. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_ResolveInputs . Retire an actor — never delete one candidate, extracted An actor id is referenced from roles, diagrams, beans and commits, so removing the file leaves every one of those unable to tell retirement from accident. Same rule, and the same reason, as a scrapped bean. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_RetireActor . Retrieve for each sub-question candidate, extracted The paper's Searcher, at the granularity A_Plan chose. Which retrieval paradigm — text-only, vision-only or hybrid — is recorded in the methodology node as an open trade-off rather than settled here: the paper's comparison was measured on its own corpus and says nothing about a folio's. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/deep-document-research.bpmn#A_Search . Retrieve the npm package or tarball candidate, extracted An npm source (schemas/kg/subgraph-source.ts, npm-kg-distribution): an npm package specifier or tarball path (.tgz). kg-retrieve-npm or npm fetches and unpacks the package contents into the declared path. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_RetrieveNpmPackage . Return for correction with annotations candidate, extracted The reviewer annotates specific passages that need correction and returns to the translator with detailed feedback. Each annotation includes: - The passage in question - What is wrong (terminology, meaning, style) - The suggested correction or reference . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_ReturnForCorrection . Review and record feedback candidate, extracted The reviewer this folio binds. authoring-document relaxes the base SME step precisely because no single lane fits every document. Review the rendered folio, not a description of it, and record the feedback. The outcome is iterate — back to authoring — or approved for the publication path. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/folio-review-publish.bpmn#Task_Review . Review increment (test behaviour) candidate, extracted Inner loop: the BA tests each delivered increment against the acceptance criteria. They do not review code — they test behaviour. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#BA_ReviewIncrement . Review requirements and impact analysis candidate, extracted The BA reviews the formal requirements and the impact analysis the agent produced. When a requirement changes a rendered surface, the BA (or the requester) also reviews the wireframe candidates, web and mobile, shown wherever the requester will look (the conversation, the issue, the pull request, or several) with staging deep links and screenshots, and chooses one before implementation starts. The agent records the choice; it never makes it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#BA_ReviewReqs . Review synthesised needs statement candidate, extracted The BA reviews what the agent synthesised and checks it against what they actually need. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#BA_ReviewNeeds . Review the adoption candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/methodology-from-source.bpmn#O_Review . Review the PR; merge or close candidate, extracted The maintainer checks that the PR writes down what the issue decided and nothing else, lets the layer's checks run, and merges or closes it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-review-adjudication.bpmn#Task_TRA_Merge . Review the preview and answer candidate, extracted Members read the preview and answer in their Blue columns, or leave them as they are when the change is right. They record the row's Disposition (Blue): Pending, Accepted, Partially accepted, Not accepted, Noted, Duplicate or Out of scope. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_AnswerPreview . Review the schema definition node candidate, extracted Does the node declare what KIND of node it is? Does a widened type carry its mirrors? Does a removed field leave a reason behind, so the next author does not re-add it in good faith? And where the node RENDERS to something the site serves — a colour, a glyph, a theme's tokens — does a Tool maintain that artefact, and does the visual fact have only one home? The node decides; the stylesheet reports. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/review-code.bpmn#Task_ReviewSchema . Review the size against its budget candidate, extracted The index flags an app over its sizeBudgetMB; the site size review reads it with the rest of the site. Over budget is a finding for the author, never a silent publish. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/web-app-publish.bpmn#A_Size . Review the Tool node candidate, extracted Does it name skills, and do they resolve? Is the mechanism it advertises the one that actually runs? Are its IRIs minted rather than written out? And the question a covered skill hides: is the COMMAND reachable, or only the skill satisfied? A skill can be served by the neighbours of its mechanism while the mechanism itself is reachable from no node, and check:tools reports it as covered and is right to. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/review-code.bpmn#Task_ReviewTool . Review the translation candidate, extracted Coverage, preserved terms and echoes are mechanical. A semantic round trip needs a back-translator that has not seen the original; where none has run, the criterion carries no verdict and that is the honest state. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-narrative.bpmn#Task_ReviewTranslation . Review translation for accuracy candidate, extracted A subject-matter expert reviews the injected translated markdown for: - Clinical/technical accuracy of terminology - Preservation of meaning from the source - Cultural appropriateness for the target locale - Consistency with the domain glossary For WHO content: the SME verifies that normative statements ("SHALL", "SHOULD", "MAY") are translated with the correct force in the target language. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_SMEReview . Review what the substrate offers candidate, extracted Every subgraph, asset class and harness the cached declaration names, each with its current state — referenced, materialised, unknown, stale, or refused by a gate. Shown whole, because a reader who sees only what was chosen cannot tell "not offered" from "not taken". BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Review . Round trip on the changed strings candidate, extracted The untainted round trip, with the sample restricted to the strings this run translated. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Call_TR_RoundTrip . Round-trip translation QA candidate, extracted Back-translate the target-language .md into the source language and compare the meaning with the original. It catches semantic drift and terminology misses that a forward-only fluency check cannot see, and tells the two apart. Tool: the translation_validate MCP tool. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_RoundTripQa . Round-trip translation QA candidate, extracted No gateway follows: drift or clean, the translation goes to Task_SMEReview with the findings attached. Which of two readings is right is a human call (translation-manager, "route drift to a human reviewer"), and every translation in this workflow is reviewed and signed off anyway, so a clean result is evidence for the reviewer and never a way around them. The findings include translation:glossary:check's: every glossary term translated against the locale term base, fixed before sign-off, with its glossary section in the KG QA report. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_RoundTripQA . Round-trip translation QA candidate, extracted Back-translate each localized narrative into its source language and compare the meaning, to catch semantic drift and bad terminology that a forward-only check cannot see. Agentic. Two parties are kept apart under untainted-verification: a back-translator that sees ONLY the target-language text, and an adjudicator that sees the original and the back-translation and rules. The verdict is recorded per block, under criterion translation-semantic-roundtrip in the block's <block>.<locale>.translation-qa.json sidecar, by the translation-roundtrip-record Tool (translation-manager §5). A terminology miss is a different criterion, translation-terms-preserved (acronyms, numbers, URLs that must survive), so Gateway_Drift can tell the two apart. Never close this step by reversing the PO's msgid→msgstr map: that returns the source exactly and scores 1.0 always. An empty translation-semantic-roundtrip entry list means "not yet run", which is never a pass. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn#Task_RoundTrip . Round-trip translation QA (back-translate) candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_RoundTripQA . Route every climb through platform.ts candidate, extracted Every platform symbol the sub-KG uses is re-exported from <name>/platform.ts, so re-pointing the platform is a one-file edit. A merge from main is where new climbs arrive; reroute them here. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Seam . Route it, and watch the queue candidate, extracted A file goes to ingestion; a link or a description goes to whatever will resolve it. Acquisition stops here — the moment a file is in the queue, library-ingestion owns it, and keeping that seam sharp is what lets a resource acquired through a channel that does not exist yet reach ingestion unchanged. An arrival may be minutes or days away, so it is watched rather than chased. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Route . Route the answer back, quoted candidate, extracted On answerRoute, with the person's own message attached by id where the host allows, so the sibling can treat it as the person's approval. A paraphrase is never approval. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#D_RouteBack . Run placement, file a bean candidate, extracted The offer produces a DECISION, not a node. placement then decides layer, graph and node kind — it is the step that catches a hardcoded path or a literal naming one folio — and the authoring itself becomes a bean, because work here is a bean before it is a file. op="note" and not create, for the reason A_CreateBeans above states: the engine has no create op — it claims, notes and resolves the instance's OWN bean. The agent mints the authoring bean itself with beans create, running the exact-title existence check first, and what this step records is a note that the decision was taken. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_RecordKg . Run the deterministic gates candidate, extracted Template currency, catalogue coverage, placeholder, tag and URL preservation, officiality, kg:locale, and the locale's supplements compiling with no SUSHI error and passing their structural checks. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_Gates . Run the node audits candidate, extracted check:tools, kg:audit and typecheck. Read the kg-qa sidecar rather than the summary: it is written per node so an inherited defect and a new one are distinguishable. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/review-code.bpmn#Task_RunNodeAudits . Run the review-log-watch check candidate, extracted Runs Tool review-log-watch with the folio repository, the saved values and the log's state file. The tool reads the repository's open and closed issues (no pull requests, no issue labelled no-sheet) and compares a digest of them and of the cells people set (Title, Selected Sections, Contributor Feedback, Disposition, Ready for agent, Ready for merge, Dispositions confirmed; on a public-comment log also Committee Feedback, TWG (CS), TWG (human), Change Set (human)) with the last check's. A read with no Issue column tracks only change-set issues and appends no rows, reporting them as issue-unlinked. It writes nothing. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn#Task_RunCheck . Run the rule's mechanical half candidate, extracted Whatever patterns and terminology the rule carries. A judgementOnly rule has no mechanical half by declaration, which is different from nobody having written one yet. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_MechanicalHalf .

7339.title: S
7339.content: Say what is being decided, and why it matters now candidate, extracted First, and in the message itself: where you are (the Process and task, as which Role, asking whom — from the three determinations), what the decision is, what depends on it, and what is already known — each fact with where it came from. Sign the package and/or each asset candidate, extracted THE TRUST ANCHOR IS GDHCN, SPECIFIED BY THE WHO SMART TRUST IG. READ OFF THAT IG rather than from general knowledge: a GDHCN trustlist distributes KEY MATERIAL as W3C DID documents, and says nothing about what you wrap your bytes in — the health-certificate envelope is a separate specification in the same IG, and a document package is not a health certificate. So what is settled is where a verifier GETS THE KEY, not what it verifies. A portal that can fetch the bytes but not reach the trustlist cannot verify, which is unknown and not a failure — air-gapped is a declared deployment value, so that case is answered rather than assumed away. Still OPEN and unread: the rotation and revocation model, and whether a document-package signature can be expressed for a GDHCN-aware verifier at all. Two schemes with different properties remain to choose between, and the trustlist does not choose between them. A PACKAGE signature over the manifest verifies the SET — nothing added, removed or altered — and must be reissued whenever any file changes. A PER-ASSET signature verifies one file independently, which is what an edge cache serving one asset can actually check, and it cannot detect a removal because there is nothing left to verify. They compose; composing them is the safer and more expensive default, and it is the deployment's choice rather than the pipeline's. 7345.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, A–D
7345.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 393 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 70 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-sci 5 (SKOS). One of 3 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 153 terms and is 133 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 897 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 897 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 153 shown . 0–9 A B C D

7346.content: 1 · Declare in place (nothing moves) candidate, extracted A <name>.json entry with its graphs[] kinds. A sub-graph that owns its own layout gains a NESTED declaration whose paths resolve against its own directory, so the whole graph relocates by moving one folder. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Declare . 2a · Measure — unassigned column FIRST candidate, extracted bun run cat check:partition. Read the unassigned column before the edge count, and quote BOTH numbers rather than only the one that improved. The edge count can rise when the measurement improves (previously unjudged edges are folded in); that is correct. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Measure . 2b · Prune, merge, factor — or the classification is wrong candidate, extracted The only four moves. Move the shared TARGET first and the importers after; check the target's layer before the importer's; a schema moves with its script. The fix is never an exemption, it is the right owner. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Move . 3 · Isolate — own declaration, namespace, artefact candidate, extracted Only once cross-edges measure zero: give the sub-graph its own declaration, its own namespace and its own published artefact, as bootstrap/ has (its own declaration, bs: namespace and graph document). Nothing moves yet; the sub-graph now stands alone in place. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Isolate . 4 · Extract — a directory move, not a file-by-file sift candidate, extracted Only once edges are zero and the declaration stands alone: move the sub-graph out as one directory move, not a file-by-file sift. Its nested declaration resolves paths against its own directory, so moving the folder moves the graph. The five-point gate is in migration-plan.md Phase II. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Extract .

7347.title: A
7347.content: Accept it, and record where it came from candidate, extracted Both branches land here. An unprompted offer is accepted as it stands — do not make somebody follow a process to hand over what they already have. Provenance is recorded whichever channel it arrived through: a description given in chat has a source and can be wrong, exactly as a PDF does. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Accept . Accept the new state candidate, extracted Runs the check again with --accept, so the state file holds what was just handled and the next poll compares against it. A row the pass could not finish stays changed and is picked up on the next poll. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn#Task_Accept . Accept, or send back candidate, extracted The editor's lane, kept separate on purpose: the reviewer who judged the change is not the position that accepts it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Task_EditorDecides . Accessibility: measure, do not assert candidate, extracted Contrast COMPUTED against the real ground, including the worst case a backdrop can present; a non-colour channel wherever colour carries meaning (SC 1.4.1); an accessible name on every region; keyboard and focus order. An automated pass is necessary and not sufficient — axe accepts a non-empty placeholder as an accessible name, and a CSS selector that matches nothing raises no error at all. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_Accessibility . Act on the answer candidate, extracted Never ask the person again for what they answered. A rule-level answer goes into the governing skill in the same turn. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#S_Act . Add an actor, and declare its kind candidate, extracted Human, agentic or mechanical. A userTask because the agentic/mechanical line is JUDGEMENT — role-model.md says so — and reading it wrong disqualifies the actor from every judgement task it exists to perform, silently. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_AddActor . Adjudicate the conflict candidate, extracted A human or agentic decision, never a merge rule. Which side wins depends on why the local edit was made, and a process that picked automatically would be choosing without the one fact that decides it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the criterion disagreement candidate, extracted The shared judgement — entry condition, untainted dispatch, person-or-agent restriction — asked with THIS question's permitted answers. cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes sits here rather than on A_Adjudicate inside it because the answers depend on what was asked, and the gateway below is what acts on them: the engine refuses a mismatch between the two. Process_Adjudication may also leave at End_NotAdjudicable — one entry and no other side is a review or a gate, not a disagreement — in which case nothing below runs and there is nothing to record. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/criterion-adjudication.bpmn#Call_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the disagreement candidate, extracted The judgement itself, and the one step nothing here can check: if a mechanism could decide it, the process would not have been entered. It declares NO cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes on purpose, and that absence is the whole of bean bvuk. This step used to name three — stands, scope, dispensation — and six diagrams called it: review-narrative and voice-review, whose question those three answer, and four whose question they do not. refresh-materialized asks which side wins a local-vs-remote conflict; there is no criterion to scope there and no dispensation to grant, yet the outcome half ran regardless. Since the caller's question decides the permitted answers, the caller declares them: cat-harness.processes:adjudication codes on its OWN call activity, with its own gateway acting on them. criterion-adjudication.bpmn is that for the QA-criterion question. What could NOT be fixed by passing the codes as data, which was this bean's first recommendation: the three branches ran three different TASKS, so a caller handed local-wins would have had it pointing at A_ScopeCriterion. The branches had to move, not the enum. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/adjudication.bpmn#A_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the flagged passage candidate, extracted A machine can detect that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-l1-completeness-gate.bpmn#Task_FlagDrift . Adjudicate the flagged passage (human) candidate, extracted A human SME or editor reviews the flagged passage. They may: - Accept the translation as-is (false positive) - Edit the translation and re-run QA - Reject and request re-translation The round trip establishes that two readings differ. Which one is right is a human call. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudicate the voice findings candidate, extracted Three outcomes, all legitimate: the register is wrong for this genre; the criterion does not belong in this genre and should carry profiles; or the block is a stated exception and a reviewer entry records why. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-narrative.bpmn#Task_AdjudicateVoice . Adjudicate: prose, scope, or exception candidate, extracted The same three outcomes as the base voice axis. The register is wrong for this block (fix the prose); the rule does not apply to this content (scope it on the voice, one edit rather than ten overrules); or the rule applies and this block is an exception (a reviewer entry saying why). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_Adjudicate . Adjudication candidate, extracted folio-assistant's adjudication: the adjudication leads, the checker's entry is kept, and the dispensation carries its reason. Reviewers disagreeing on ONE criterion is a criterion disagreement, so this calls the QA-criterion specialisation: the failing entry stands, the criterion does not apply to this screen, or a dispensation is granted with its reason. The entry condition matches exactly rather than approximately: GW_Agree asks whether the blind reviewers' entries agree and takes no here, and Process_CriterionAdjudication starts at "entries for one criterion disagree" — R_Review records pass, warn or fail PER CRITERION with a reason, so the disagreement reaching this step is a per-criterion disagreement between reviewer entries and nothing else. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#Call_Adjudicate . Agent pass on the changed rows candidate, extracted For each changed row, the agent pass of Contributor feedback on a working draft: Ready for agent = Yes gets its edit, Ready for merge = Yes its merge, and a Blue answer to a Decision needed question is taken up. Every new row (from an issue, a person or a TWG workbook), every row with an empty Feedback (agent) and every row whose Blue cells changed gets feedback in the same wake, in the fixed layout: the ask first (Decision needed: with lettered options, one recommended, and where to answer), then Proposed direction: and Next:, only the tags bold. The work stays inside the row's Selected Sections; a row with none gets a question asking which, and any edit outside them is named on an Outside the selected sections: line. PRs are named as repo#n, which the sheet script links, and it adds a Where to review line linking each selected section on the preview. The agent then runs tools/review-log-watch/lint.ts and fixes what it flags: a cell that breaks the layout, or a PR state that GitHub contradicts. The agent records its step on the Agent tab at once, with the real time. Previews follow main: by default (Config PREVIEW_REFRESH automatic) the agent runs tools/review-log-watch/previews.ts on every poll for every open change-set PR, and also when people act on a change set (new Blue feedback, Ready for agent set to Yes, or feedback asking to update the preview); with PREVIEW_REFRESH on-feedback, only then. A branch behind main gets main merged in (a merge commit), pushed and restaged; a conflict a person must settle is asked in the change set's feedback. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn#Task_AgentPass . Announce the branch on the issue candidate, extracted On CREATING the feature branch, comment on the issue: the branch name, the process and phase, and the beans claimed. Visibility is the whole point — without it a sibling session or a human cannot tell that work has begun, only that it has finished. Deliberately on this edge and not inside Phase 6. The three loops back into A_Implement (increment rejected, MVP not ready, feedback translated) re-enter implementation on the SAME branch, and re-announcing on each would be noise. Announce once, when the branch is created. Before announcing, run the collision review that starts any new unit of work (coordinate, "Starting new work"): open PRs and in-progress beans checked against the branch's files and subject, scaled to the blast radius, and the result recorded in the bean before the first edit. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_AnnounceBranch . Answer the other four gates candidate, extracted Restrictions, copyright, retention and source loss, each answered permitted, refused or unknown. They are four answers to one decision, and Gateway_Gates reads them with size through decisions/materialization-gate.dmn. RESTRICTIONS. 'No restrictions known in context' is a STATE, not a green light. GateVerdict is three-valued for this reason alone, and unknown is never rendered as permitted. COPYRIGHT. What the licence permits for THIS bitstream, and separately whether it permits the derivation. LICENSE-CONTENT.md exists in this repository and the ingestion pipeline does not read it. RETENTION. A copy with no expiry cannot be told from an abandoned one — the same argument bean-blocking makes about a block with no expiry. An ARCHIVAL copy is the exception and it is a specification rather than an omission: freshness() reports it permanent, not no-expiry. SOURCE LOSS. Not hypothetical. The one IRIS record this repository holds carries a handle on iris.wpro.who.int, a regional instance merged into the global one. Only an ARCHIVAL copy of the original bytes discharges this; a working copy cannot, because the derived sections are not the publication. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_AnswerGates . Answer, decline, or say nothing candidate, extracted The Requestor's move. Declining is an answer. Saying nothing is not, and is what the recommendation's "if there is no answer" was for. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_Answer . Append removed with the reason candidate, extracted BEFORE the removal, not after: a job that dies mid-step must leave a record of the intent rather than an artefact that vanished with no entry. A reason is REQUIRED — an entry saying an artefact went and not why is the ambiguity this log exists to prevent. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/staging-render-log.bpmn#A_LogRemoved . Append rendered candidate, extracted A re-deploy is a rendering, so it gets its own entry rather than overwriting the last. "When was this last built" is then answerable without diffing commits. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/staging-render-log.bpmn#A_LogRendered . Append restored candidate, extracted A full-replace deploy (docs-site.yml, the only publisher without keep_files) wipes the branch; restore-staging carries the previews AND this log back in. Its own event rather than a second rendered, because "somebody pushed this branch" and "an unrelated merge nearly deleted it" are different facts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/staging-render-log.bpmn#A_LogRestored . Append retained with the reason candidate, extracted Records that a removal was considered and refused, or that a preview still stands because a signal fired; without the entry that leaves no trace, and nobody can tell why a preview is still up. A reason is REQUIRED — the tool refuses without one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_LogRetained . Append retained with the reason candidate, extracted Records that a removal was considered and refused, or that a preview still stands because a signal fired; without the entry that leaves no trace, and nobody can tell why a preview is still up. A reason is REQUIRED — the tool refuses without one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/staging-render-log.bpmn#A_LogRetained . Append every suggestion as a human candidate candidate, extracted Every suggestion, whoever filed it, is appended to the catalogue's translation-candidates/v1 sidecar as {kind: "human", id: "github:<login>", by, issue}, with the msgidHash of the string it translates and its placeholder QA. A proposal is never refused for a changed catalogue and never conflicts with another: the sidecar keeps them all, ranked side by side. A record that does not parse, or that names another repository or another translations directory, is refused here. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-review-adjudication.bpmn#Task_TRA_Propose . Append rows for new issues; hide closed ones candidate, extracted For each row in the tool's append list (one per issue that no row's Issue cell links yet), appends it below the last row of Contributor Feedback: Title is the issue's title, the first Contributor Feedback column @login (#N): the issue's first paragraph, Issue its URL. The script gives each new row its Change-set id. No other writer adds issue rows. Then each row linking a closed issue (the tool's closedRows, and the rows just appended as closed) is hidden and its text struck through. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn#Task_AppendRows . Append WHO disclaimer (if DAK) candidate, extracted For WHO SMART Guidelines content, automatically appends the WHO legal disclaimer: - Translation not created by WHO - English edition is authoritative original - WHO not responsible for translation accuracy Only applies when folio contentType includes WHO/DAK content. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_AppendDisclaimer . Apply it, and state each option's trade-offs candidate, extracted Follow the selected methodology as written — adopted whole, not blended with another. At least two real options: one option is not a choice, and a straw option is worse than a short list because it makes the analysis look thorough while narrowing it. Never quantify the comparison to make it look measured. Where a method scores and sums, this platform takes the structure and refuses the arithmetic: the weights are invented and a total reads as a measurement. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/options-analysis.bpmn#A_Apply . Apply the stated default, and say so candidate, extracted Only the default stated in A_Recommend, only where the caller allows one, and recorded as assumed with the default named — never as the person's answer. The next message to the person says it was applied, so they can reverse it. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_ApplyDefault . Approve requirements candidate, extracted Stakeholders approve the requirements and impact analysis on the issue, or send them back for revision. Only their approval moves the work to sign-off; an agent never records an approval on a person's behalf. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#S_ApproveReqs . ARCHIVAL verify fixity — never re-fetch candidate, extracted Re-compute the digest and compare. An archive is NEVER re-fetched — the source is what it exists to survive, so replacing it with today's version discards the state it was keeping. A mismatch means OUR copy rotted, and the remedy is restoration from a backup, not re-download. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_Fixity . Archive → greppable contents manifest candidate, extracted NOT IMPLEMENTED; see docs/document-ingestion.md. Tar/zip is opaque to every grep in the corpus until its contents are listed as data. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-derive-content.bpmn#Task_Archive . Ask BA to create or link issue candidate, extracted Ask — never create. Creating an issue without the BA's permission is the thing this step exists to prevent. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-issue-linking.bpmn#A_AskCreate . Ask first about what could not be determined candidate, extracted The caller's question waits, and is counted ("one more question after this"). What is put first is the undetermined one: the context you could not establish, the Role you are not sure you hold, or the Process you cannot place this in. It goes through the same order as any question — say what you determined and what you could not, the candidates you see, the one you would pick and why — and it allows NO default: a Process or Role assumed rather than confirmed is an authority nobody gave. With more than one undetermined, ask about the outermost first (the Process before the Role before the context), since the outer answer usually settles the inner. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_AskUndeterminedFirst . Ask for a link or a description candidate, extracted Both forms, named together. A person who cannot find the file often knows exactly what it is, and a description in their own words is an acquired resource rather than a consolation prize. Asking for the upload first demands the one thing they may not have, before the cheaper answers have been offered. Say what happens if they do nothing. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/content-acquisition.bpmn#A_Ask . Ask ONE question candidate, extracted One question, answerable by picking. With several decisions open, ask one in full and give a count for the rest. Uses whatever channel the caller is in — in bootstrap, the conversation the person is already in. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_PutQuestion . Ask the person candidate, extracted A step the agent cannot do or cannot check from here — switching Pages on without a signed-in gh, granting a permission, choosing between two ways of fixing a declaration. Asked through the one reusable discussion, with the exact step written out so it can be followed without opening anything else. A person saying "done" is recorded as their word, not as a check; the next run checks it. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_AskPerson . Ask the person candidate, extracted The sibling's ask, unchanged in letters and recommendation, through Process_AskThePerson: the full chat text first, naming the sibling and that the answer will be passed on, then the card. A tap on the sibling's own card or a Blue-column answer in the sheet answers it too; take the first. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#D_Ask . Ask to authorise the extraction candidate, extracted A repository cut changes the substrate every other process binds to; that is a person's decision. Declining leaves the graph declared, detangled, isolated and split in place. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-authorise.bpmn#Task_Authorise . Ask to freeze the in-repo copy candidate, extracted The agent reports the files that would move, their size, the new repository and the commit the copy matches, then asks: (1) freeze it in the kept trashcan now, (2) keep in place until the first release, (3) show the file list first. Default if there is no answer: (2), nothing moves. A green fresh clone is the precondition for asking, not the answer. Non-relaxable. The host keeps a FROZEN copy in the kept trashcan, not a refreshed mirror and not a deletion; the live copy is the remote mount or subscription set up at stage 10. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_ConfirmCutover . Ask whether it should leave now candidate, extracted The owner decides, from what is measured, whether the sub-KG starts staging for separation now. Asked as numbered options with the recommended one first and a stated default: keeping it in place is the default, and is a real outcome. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_DecideLeave . Ask whether to separate it candidate, extracted The owner decides from the measured signals, and also decides the address base for its identifiers, where verdicts about it live, and what its tools repository owns. Declining is a real outcome: the graph stays where it is. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Decide . Ask which harness, and where candidate, extracted The candidates go in as the options; the recommendation may name one; the default is NONE. What A_DetermineWhere established goes in too — the process, the two roles, the context — so the called discussion checks it rather than re-deriving it; and anything it could not establish goes in as undetermined, to be asked first. The Requestor's answer comes back as answered, or the question as still open. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_AskRequestor . Ask who is acting candidate, extracted The one step that needs a person. Asked ONCE and recorded, never re-asked: memory/interaction.json and the record exist so that a preference stated once is not requested again, which is WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/session-state-machine.bpmn#A_AskWhoIsActing . Assign to qualified human translator candidate, extracted The coordinator assigns the translation to a qualified translator, ideally a domain SME for the content area. For WHO content, the translator should be familiar with WHO SMART Guidelines terminology. The assignment includes: - The .pot file(s) from extraction - The domain glossary - Context notes (block kind, chapter, content area) - The deadline . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/human-translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_AssignTranslator . Audit the code nodes the increment adds candidate, extracted Descend into the review task for what this increment CHANGED IN THE GRAPH — Tool definitions in tools/ and schema definition nodes under schemas/. It runs before the summary, and therefore before an MVP can be shared: a Tool or schema node shipped in an MVP is the version stakeholders start building expectations on, and a node that names a skill nobody wrote is cheaper to catch here than after sign-off. Called, not inherited: the agent keeps its implementing role and takes on the code-reviewer lane inside Process_CodeReview for that call path only. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#A_CodeAudit . Audit the graph candidate, extracted AFTER the change, not before. Every criterion here is a join — role to lane, actor to role, activity to skill — so what an administrative edit breaks is not in the file it edited. The sidecars under test/results/kg-qa/ are committed for the reason a printed verdict is not: without them, "unbound since it was drawn" and "broken by this change" are indistinguishable. Runs kg:audit. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_RunKgAudit . Authorise the extraction candidate, extracted The one step no package may relax. A repository cut changes the substrate every other diagram's lanes bind to, and that is a person's decision. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/graph-detanglement.bpmn#Task_Authorise . Authorise the extraction candidate, extracted Report what moves and ask the administrator. A repository cut changes the substrate every other process binds to; that is a person's decision. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Call_Authorise . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Call_Authorise . Auto-pick by rank candidate, extracted For each string nobody has adjudicated, its candidates are ranked: official 0, adjudicated 1, a person's proposal 2, a translation platform (Weblate, Crowdin, Transifex) 3, an agent model 4, machine translation 5; a QA failure adds 10; ties go to the newest; a stale candidate, made for another source text, is never picked. An empty msgstr, or one that is itself an earlier auto-pick, takes the best: fuzzy and unofficial (chosen.how: auto), except an official candidate whose English matches the msgid exactly, which is written as auto-official. A collaborator's choice, and text whose provenance is not an auto-pick, are never overwritten. translation-strings.ts applyAutoPick; the 🌐 pane ranks with the same function's rules. Precedence, within one subject area (the scheme's subject): the more authoritative (lower) layer fixes a term's translation; a layer only adds. A match in another subject area is a sense check, not a violation. Each layer's glossary is the directory it declares with the glossary graph typology. 7349.content: Categorize and summarize candidate, extracted Each hit gets a category (overlaps: coordinate; affected by; out of scope; unrelated) and a one-line summary with its state. Judgement, not a keyword score: say why each is in its category. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/related-work.bpmn#A_Categorize . Check AtomicMass.lean is in sync candidate, extracted Run gen_atomic_mass.py --check: regenerate AtomicMass.lean from the data table and diff it against the committed file. Any divergence exits 1 with a unified diff and fails the PR — a Lean file that compiles must not carry numbers the table no longer produces. Check each page; OCR pages that fail candidate, extracted Owner, 2026-11-11 (who-iris, card Q-ODD-1 = A): "force OCR when a page's text layer fails a quality check". A text layer can hold plenty of letters and still not be the page's text: accents mapped to Greek letters ("dΘclaration"), Persian set in the wrong Arabic code points, words split by kerning ("au g m ente"), fake-bold words printed twice, mojibake. cat-harness-tools scripts/_text_quality.py checks every page against the document's languages (dc.language.iso, or --lang-hint); the router then OCRs the document and pdf-structure.py --ocr takes the OCR text for the failing pages only, listing them in structure.json source.ocr_pages with the reason. When most pages of a document with no outline fail, the whole document is read from OCR, as for a scan. Method: skill l1-document-ingestion, "A text layer that is not text". BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-extract-structure.bpmn#Task_PageCheck . Check glossary consistency candidate, extracted translation:glossary:check, against the layered term base: the normative reference glossaries first, then each layer in the order the index config lists it, the layer's own glossary last and never overriding. A platform term found in text of another subject area is a sense check for a person, not a violation. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_Glossary . Check glossary terms (translation:glossary:check) candidate, extracted After translating: run translation:glossary:check --instance <dir> --locale <locale>, fix the violations, and include its glossary section in the KG QA report. A term translated against the term base is a terminology miss, so it takes the drift branch to the adjudicator. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_GlossaryCheck . Check it candidate, extracted Look, do not remember. The answer is one of the four states, and "could not determine" is its own answer: a check that could not look is not a pass. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_CheckStep . Check pages are current, links resolve candidate, extracted The generator's check mode regenerates in memory and fails on any difference from the committed pages, and on any source link that does not resolve. It runs in CI, so a change to an extraction or a library entry that was not republished fails the build rather than leaving a page that says something the extraction no longer does. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/publish-extracted-statements.bpmn#Task_CheckCurrent . Check staleness (source hash) candidate, extracted On source content change: computes sha256(source.md) and compares to each translation's status.json sourceHash. If they differ, sets stale: true. The translation remains visible with a "stale — needs re-adjudication" indicator. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_StalenessCheck . Check the declaration and translations candidate, extracted Tool web-app-build (web-apps:build --check): the manifest parses, package.json has the build script, a lockfile pins exact versions, no two layers claim one app id, every template is current, and no translation drops or adds a {placeholder}. Untranslated strings are reported, not failed: the app falls back to the source text per string. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/web-app-publish.bpmn#A_Check . Check the JSON Schemas and JSON-LD are at their IRIs candidate, extracted THE PRIMARY STEP of initializing a Knowledge Graph harness and so the first one checked once the declarations are read. Every JSON Schema the harness publishes (its $id) and every JSON-LD document (its vocabulary, its diagram vocabulary, its graph export, each carrying its own @context) is at the address it names under iriBase, where a program following the IRI finds it. Two checks: that the site build stages each one at its address, and that each address answers. A 404 is not published; a 403 or no answer from here could not be determined. The Pages site is the vehicle: when the documents are not yet answering, the site steps below are how they get there, and the report leads with this step's state. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_CheckDocuments . Check the model parses and resolves candidate, extracted Tool archimate-check (archimate:validate, on the layer root): every model the config names is held and parses, every box in every view draws an element the model holds, every relationship's ends are in the model. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/archimate-publish.bpmn#A_Check . Check the selected methodology's evidence base candidate, extracted Before applying a methodology, establish that the thing being applied is what it claims to be. A methodology is adopted because it is somebody else's named, external work; this step checks that the origin it cites resolves to a source in a declared library, and reads the methodology-evidence QA sidecar for it. WHY THE CHECK IS HERE AND NOT AT ADOPTION. Adoption happens once; selection happens every time a decision is made. A source that was reachable when the methodology was adopted can stop being so, and a methodology adopted before this axis existed was never checked at all. Measured 2026-09-22: six methodologies cited an origin and NONE had that source in any library, so every selection made until then rested on an unverifiable citation. WHAT A GAP DOES AND DOES NOT DO. A missing source does NOT block the decision, and this step has no branch that stops the process — that would make a documentation gap into an outage, and the owner decides whether an unbacked methodology may still be used. It does two things: it runs literature-search to try to close the gap, and it puts the evidence state into the record A_Record writes, so a reader can tell a decision made on a verified method from one made on a citation nobody could follow. The third state is the one that matters. "Source ingested", "source located but unreachable from here" and "no source found" are three different facts, and literature-search exists largely to stop the middle one being reported as the last. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/options-analysis.bpmn#A_CheckEvidence . Check translation completeness candidate, extracted Verify that all msgid entries have msgstr translations. A requirement whose whole content is carried by the code becomes a commit and nothing else; a graph that acquires a node for it is a graph with a node nobody will ever read. The default creates NOTHING. An agent that decides on its own that a requirement "is really a skill" has manufactured a node nobody asked for, in a graph somebody else maintains — which is what this step exists to prevent. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-derive-content.bpmn#Task_Provenance . This is the only decision the generic lane makes on its own: everything after it is made inside a subprocess by the role that lane binds. Binds content-review, the same skill as Task_Consolidate in this lane, because a paper skill belongs to the science layer, which this harness diagram cannot reach. A paper process that wants semantic scoping adds it by calling this process. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Task_ClassifyChange . Close issue ONLY on BA authorisation candidate, extracted Reachable only through BA_Confirm, which is the BA saying every criterion is met. An agent must never close an issue without that explicit authorisation — the gate is the preceding task, and this name says so rather than leaving a reader to trace the flow for it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-close.bpmn#A_Close . Close the change set: the issue, then the sheet row candidate, extracted Closing is one step with two tools, GitHub and the review sheet. The agent closes the change set's issue on GitHub, with the merge or the reason it closed unmerged, then records Agentic status Closed (or Change merged) on the Agent tab through Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn). The sheet script then hides the row and strikes the whole row through ("make sure complete changeset rows are hidden so not cluttered and that text of that whole row is crossed out"). The agent never hides or strikes a row by hand, and never deletes one: reopening the issue and writing a new status shows it again. Hiding and striking are formatting only, which the review-log watcher ignores. A change set closed without a merge, at a person's request, takes this step too. It does NOT resolve beans or complete instances: those outlive the session by design, and a machine that closed them on the way out would be asserting work finished because somebody went away.
