BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Call_CodeReview . Cold start: mount and attach candidate, extracted Lay down every pinned layer from each layer's lock, as its AGENTS.md cold start says, and attach each repository the run will change. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_ColdStart . Collect each statement with its source section candidate, extracted For every statement extracted from the library entries the artifact draws on, read three things off files: the statement verbatim, the library entry it came from, and the section of that entry, as a library reference (layer, library id, section id). The section's label is read from the entry's structure: its title and its locator in the source's own unit (a slide, a page, a cell range, a line range). For example "Catch up schedule, slide 7". A statement whose section cannot be resolved is NOT published without a link: it is reported, because a statement nobody can trace is the failure this process exists to prevent. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/publish-extracted-statements.bpmn#Task_Collect . Comment why nothing was recorded candidate, extracted Every refusal, with its reason, as a comment on the issue (exit 3). No pull request is opened. A refusal is never a partial record dressed as a whole one; a new review is a new issue and a new instance of this process. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-review-adjudication.bpmn#Task_TRA_Refuse . Compare what the processes need with what is granted candidate, extracted The needed set is the agent-permissions skill's list (write generated projections: CI only, never the agent; edit hooks or settings; run the gates; push a feature branch; open a PR), scoped to what this layer's processes actually call. The granted set is the recorded grants plus the Tool's current config, read through its adapter. A config rule with no recorded grant is reported as unrecorded, not treated as granted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/secure-agent-permissions.bpmn#Task_ReadGrants . Compose each harness's nav and tile candidate, extracted One themed section per layer in dependency order, from its declaration: its docs, its declared subgraphs (a graph with no viewer is shown inert and labelled), and its theme. Written to _data/harness.json by sync-docs-harness.ts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/harness-default-rendering.bpmn#A_Tiles . Compose the full question candidate, extracted What is being decided, stated as what will differ; every id, path and coined name glossed; every option with its letter, a one-line explanation and its trade-off; the recommendation, first and marked; what will happen if no answer comes. Can the reader answer without opening anything? If not, it is not ready. More than one decision open: ask the next one in full and give a count for the rest. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/ask-the-person.bpmn#A_Compose . Compose the hand-back and post it in own thread candidate, extracted Compose it once, against the input schema: a question is the full ask-the-person input (what will differ, context, lettered options with a one-line trade-off each, the recommendation, what happens with no answer); context, a result or a blocker gets the same stand-alone test. Post it in your own thread too, chat text then card. Your own thread is never the only copy. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#S_Compose . Compose the message candidate, extracted Five required strings — timestamp, actor, process, task, message — and one optional markdown body. The five are required because each answers a question a reader of the log will otherwise have to guess, and a guessed answer in a log is worse than a missing one. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/log-message.bpmn#A_Compose . Confirm all criteria met candidate, extracted The business analyst confirms every acceptance criterion from the requirements is met. The issue closes only on their authorisation — an agent never closes an issue on its own say-so. It IS an adjudication with the requirement-set answers: an approval here moves the set to accepted, which check:requirements refuses unless it is a human's and every approved member is in-force. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-close.bpmn#BA_Confirm . Confirm needs statement candidate, extracted Stakeholders confirm, on the issue, that the needs statement says what they need — or say what to change. A stakeholder's judgement; an agent does not record it for them. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#S_ConfirmNeeds . Confirm the cardinalities candidate, extracted An operational question, asked of the people who run the process because they know where the exceptions are. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#S_ConfirmCardinality . Confirm the entities are the ones meant candidate, extracted A naming question. The BA owns the domain vocabulary; the agent does not guess, which is CRDM's own rule for phase 1 and applies here with more force. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#BA_ConfirmEntities . Consolidate findings candidate, extracted One report from however many subprocesses ran. Findings are advice: a reviewer cannot accept the change. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Task_Consolidate . Contributor feedback candidate, extracted Process_ContributorFeedback: while the document is a working draft, the Authoring Committee gives feedback through the Contributor Feedback sheet, and each change set is edited and merged in its own pull request. When its changes are merged, the document is validated and rendered again. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/folio-review-publish.bpmn#Call_ContributorFeedback . Coordinate? How? candidate, extracted The asset carries no description. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/related-work.bpmn#U_Coordinate . Copy asset into target folio and declare in assets[] candidate, extracted Write the asset bytes into a declared path inside the target folio and add the KgAsset entry to the target folio's <name>.json assets[] list (directory-conventions). Never drop the copy into an undeclared scratch directory. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/copy-into-folio.bpmn#Task_CopyAndDeclareAsset . Create the declared state branch if missing candidate, extracted A state branch the root layer declares and its own remote lacks is created by bun run cat state:seed --init, seeded empty with the standard layout. The layer that declares a state branch creates it at initialization (owner, 2026-11-17): state:mount, the session-start hook and a new layer's scaffold all run this step. The seed is a state-manifest/v1 manifest with authoritative: true, a README, and the graph's starting files. A branch that exists is left as it is, and no branch is pushed onto an empty remote, where it would become the default branch. A MOUNTED layer's branch is never created from a downstream checkout: its miss names that layer's repository and the command to run there. Where the token cannot push, the mount stops with one line naming state:seed --init, rather than three gates failing downstream. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_CreateStateBranch . Create the repositories candidate, extracted The owner creates the content and tools repositories and their Pages. Nothing is committed to them before this. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-move.bpmn#Task_Create . Cross the axes into SO, WO, ST, WT candidate, extracted The TOWS matching step, and the only step that produces anything actionable. Strengths and weaknesses across, opportunities and threats down, and each cell names the strategy the pairing implies: SO — achieve opportunities that greatly match the strengths; WO — overcome weaknesses to attain opportunities; ST — use strengths to reduce vulnerability to threats; WT — prevent weaknesses, to avoid becoming more susceptible to threats. A SWOT that stops at four lists is the failure the source names as its central one. This step is what the process exists to reach. It produces CANDIDATE strategies, not a chosen one, and they are not ranked — see the process documentation on why no scoring activity exists. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_Cross . Cut over candidate, extracted Retire the parent's copy and measure the cutover until it is complete or cannot be shown complete. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Call_Cutover . Cut over candidate, extracted Freeze the in-repo copy in the kept trashcan and measure the cutover until it is complete or cannot be shown complete. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Call_Cutover . Cut the subgraph that leaves candidate, extracted Apply the editorial scope mechanically and report what it removed. A selection that reports nothing cannot be told from one that ran over an empty rule. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#A_Select . Cutover: retire the parent's copy candidate, extracted The one commit worth reverting, made only after the parent consumes the release and every identifier dereferences. It retires the parent's copy, frozen, never refreshed and never rendered, rather than deleting it. Where the copy goes is the sub-kg-lifecycle skill's stage 13; this diagram does not name that store, because the published graph must not. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-cutover.bpmn#Task_Cutover .

7350.title: D
7350.content: Data model Entities + cardinalities candidate, extracted Between requirements and sign-off, and the order is the argument: requirements are statements about things, and the model says what the things ARE. Drafted earlier it is invented from nothing, since the entities come from the phase-2 BPA; drafted later, sign-off approves requirements whose nouns were never pinned — which is how two stakeholders approve one sentence meaning different things. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_DataModel . Decide what may leave the repository candidate, extracted EDITORIAL, and it is stage 1 rather than a filter bolted to the exporter. kg-export produces the WHOLE graph because inspection wants the whole graph; a portal wants what its readers may see. Running the second as the first is how a QA verdict, a bean's blocking note or an unpublished draft reaches a public cache. Decided once, here, rather than at each consumer. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#E_Scope . Declare it in place, with its seam candidate, extracted <name>/<name>.json with name, version, repository (the planned home), livesAt (where it sits today), needs, and only the directories that exist, each declared with its files in one commit. <name>/platform.ts from the first commit, so no climb out of the directory ever needs rerouting. Scaffolded by init-folio --staged <path>, which writes those two files and nothing at the host root; never --instance, which writes a whole repository. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Task_Declare . Declare the model where a tool can read it candidate, extracted A model in prose is a proposal; a model in the declaration is a model. Ship a reader in the same change: a model that is only documentation goes inert. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-data-model.bpmn#A_Declare . Declare the mount: harness, repository, pin candidate, extracted A layer { name, source: { remote: { repository, ref } } } in the downstream's root index.config.json, written through writeDeclaredMounts. A folio with no index still reads remoteMounts on its declaration; both at once is refused. ref is a full 40-character commit. Overrides, if any, are keyed by layer name and then by directory id — never by path. The index itself is the index-config skill's. Decide first whether you want a remote mount at all: reading another graph without holding its code is a SUBSCRIPTION, not a mount. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-dependency.bpmn#Task_DeclareMount . Declare the node materialized candidate, extracted The node's state moves from referenced to materialized, carrying purpose, localPath, gates and (archival) fixity. There is NO default state: a node that has not said is invalid, because 'the author did not say' and 'the author said they could not tell' are different facts. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Declare . Declare the purpose: working or archival candidate, extracted working or archival, and it is asked FIRST because three of the five gates mean different things under each. An archival copy keeps the original bytes, never expires, requires fixity, and is the only thing that discharges sourceLoss; a working copy keeps derived content and discharges none of that. A process that gated first and asked afterwards would be judging a copy whose obligations it did not yet know. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_Purpose . Declare the web-app directory candidate, extracted The layer declares a directory of kind web-app in its <name>.json and puts a web-app.json (web-app/0.1.0) at its root: id, title, description, how it builds, the languages it ships (the site's six UN languages: ar, en, es, fr, ru, zh), the layer directories it reads at build time (contentFrom), a size budget, and for a copied app its licence and source. Its UI strings are one flat catalog in the source language (i18n.catalog). No publish script, no site.build.keep, no harness of its own. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/web-app-publish.bpmn#A_Declare . Declare, detangle, isolate candidate, extracted The graph-detanglement practice, all of its gates: declared in place, zero wrong-direction edges on every axis, and standing alone with its own declaration, namespace and artefact. A plain task on purpose, not a call to graph-detanglement.bpmn: that process ends in its own authorise-and-extract steps, which here are stages 9-13 of this one, and calling it would run them twice. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Detangle . Deduplicate, and keep what is actually relevant candidate, extracted The paper's Refiner. Accumulates into the evidence set the report is built from — so what is dropped here is invisible downstream, which is why it is a step somebody performs rather than a filter buried in retrieval. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/deep-document-research.bpmn#A_Refine . Deploy the MVP to staging candidate, extracted An MVP is shared AS A branches/ DEPLOY, not as a description of one. feature-staging.yml publishes the branch under branches/<branch-slug>/ on gh-pages and comments the URL on the PR, so the stakeholder who tests it is looking at the built artefact rather than at a screenshot — the same argument the merge discipline makes about rendered work: holding a rendered change back for assessment makes assessment harder, not safer. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#A_DeployStaging . Deploy the rendering candidate, extracted publish-site.ts commits the staged tree onto gh-pages as a full replace (run by the instance's Pages workflow on a push to main, or by an agent with its own git credentials); GitHub Pages then builds it from the branch. Rebuild and retry on a rejected push; never rebase the branch. The report names the gh-pages commit SHA. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_Deploy . Derive the metamodel in use candidate, extracted Tool archimate-metamodel (archimate:metamodel --check, on the layer root): the element types the model uses and every (source type, relationship, target type) pattern, each checked against ArchiMate's relationship table. Placeholder elements named after their own type are reported, never fatal: removing them is the author's call. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/archimate-publish.bpmn#A_Metamodel . Describe the need (chat, issue, discussion) candidate, extracted The BA describes the capability gap in their own words. They do not need to know it is called CRDM. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#BA_Submit . Detect feature request (crdm-detect skill) candidate, extracted Recognise the request as a platform capability change rather than content work, from crdm-detect's signals. Never call it "CRDM" to the person. Mid-content-work, ask whether to pause for requirements now or record a work item for later — do not switch on your own. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#A_Detect . Detect what moved candidate, extracted translation:status --instance <root> for new, obsolete and fuzzy strings, and the instance's template check. Either failing, or showing anything but zero, is a change. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_Detect . Determine the context: what is known, and already decided candidate, extracted Before composing anything: what is already known, each fact with where it came from; which declaration governs the matter (the layer's <name>.json, the diagram the caller is in, the Skill its task names); what state is recorded; and whether the question has ALREADY been decided — by the person earlier in the conversation, or in a declaration that quotes their ruling. A settled question is not asked again: asking it reopens a decision and spends the person's attention twice. Read it, do not remember it: cite what you read. What the caller handed in is checked here, not re-derived. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineContext . Determine the process and task, or that you are idle candidate, extracted Name the Process, the lane and the task the question belongs to, and say so in the message: "Process: Initialize a harness, at Determine the harness and repositories, as the Bootstrapping Agent". A reader who does not know which process you are in will assume the last one's rules still hold. If you are in no Process, that is an answer too: you are IDLE, and what you are doing is classifying a request to find the Process it belongs to — say that, rather than presenting a question as though a step had asked for it. You are OUT of process, and it is undetermined, when you cannot name the Process, when two candidates fit, when the step you believed was next is not the one the diagram enables, or when the work in hand was not what you said you would do. Do not infer your way back in. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineProcess . Determine the roles: which you act as, and the person's candidate, extracted An Actor performs a task in a Process AS a Role. Nothing is a Role by nature: the same agent is the Bootstrapping Agent in one diagram and another Role in the next, and which one it is depends on the lane of the task it is performing now. So say which Role you are acting as — the lane of the CALLING task, since this lane is variable — and which Role the person you ask holds (the Requestor, or whoever the calling lane names). It decides what you may ask them for: only the Requestor chooses a harness, and a question put to somebody who does not hold the decision gets an answer that settles nothing. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineRoles . Determine where you are: process, roles, context candidate, extracted Before narrowing, say where this is happening, in the words you will use in the question. PROCESS: Initialize a harness, at its first step, inside Determine the harness and repositories — the only place a Bootstrapping Agent can be (FR-2). If you cannot say that (you were started some other way, or a step you believed done is not), you are out of process: do not infer your way back in. ROLES: you act as the Bootstrapping Agent because you were told so; the person you will ask is the Requestor — the one who asked for the harness, and the only one who may choose it. A request relayed by somebody else leaves the Requestor undetermined. CONTEXT: what the request said, and what the checkout holds — a declaration at its root, a harness named in the request. Whatever cannot be determined is handed to the called discussion as undetermined, and asked about first; it is never filled with a default. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_DetermineWhere . Determine which CDN, the root URL and the Subgraphs candidate, extracted Every Subgraph id asked for must be one the declaration lists; none means the whole graph. The root URL is the one given. The target's Tool is the one that satisfies: ["render-kg-to-cdn"] for that CDN — gh-pages for GitHub Pages. A caller that already rendered and verified its tree hands the tree over instead of the graph, and the Tool pushes it without rendering again. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/render-kg-to-cdn.bpmn#Task_Resolve . Determine which harness, and where candidate, extracted The candidates are listed and the Requestor is asked, in discussion, which asks through human-agent-discussion. IN: nothing but the context this agent was handed. OUT: zero or ONE harness, and the locations — a document conforming to discussion.output.schema.json. One at most: a list of two is not an answer, and the Bootstrapping Agent may not break the tie itself. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_DetermineHarness . Discuss it with the person candidate, extracted Bootstrap's human-agent discussion, given the composed question. Its Ask ONE question step is where this harness's delivery rule applies: Post the whole composed question as ordinary chat text BEFORE any card. This is the copy that survives: a card, once answered, shows only the chosen option, and a dismissed card shows nothing. Never "see the card", never a request for a typed reply such as "1y 2n". Then the card: Whatever the host calls its selection tool (AskUserQuestion, request_decision, a button card): the same letters and labels as the chat text, the recommended option marked. No host card tool: say so in the chat and keep each answer to one short choice. Its answer step: One tap on the card, or any answer the person prefers to give. Free text is always available and never required. A dismissal is NOT an answer and never selects the default as a choice; the question stays open in the chat. On an answer: Hand the answer back to the calling step, quoted. If it settles how a kind of thing is decided, it is a rule: write it into the governing skill in the same turn. On no answer: Do what the question said would happen with no answer, and say so. Nothing irreversible proceeds on a default: such a step waits for the person. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/ask-the-person.bpmn#Call_Discuss . Dispatch with adjudicator_sees — never the artefact candidate, extracted UntaintedDispatch on the criterion declares what each party is given; the caller names a subject and a criterion and does not hand-assemble a brief, because the party composing a brief by hand is the producer. untaintedPartitionDefects reports overlap when the checker and the adjudicator can read the same file — one of them is then grading its own input, and the verdict measures nothing while raising no error. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/adjudication.bpmn#A_Dispatch . Do it, then check again candidate, extracted Only what the agent, or a tool it has, can do without replacing anything somebody wrote: regenerate a README section, add a missing Pages workflow, switch Pages on with an authenticated gh. Performing is not the same as done: the flow goes back to the check, and only the check says done. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_PerformStep . Drain: land, close or re-target the open PRs candidate, extracted Work the PRs seed:ready named until the source settles: land or close the heavy movers and the next layer's PRs, bring the layer's open PRs to five or fewer, and finish any move in flight. Fix a red rehearsal or a discovery miss where it is. Nothing is seeded from here; it goes back to the gateway, which re-asks. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_Drain . Drain: land, close or re-target the open PRs candidate, extracted Work the PRs seed:ready named until the source settles: land or close the heavy movers and the next layer's PRs, bring the layer's open PRs to five or fewer, and finish any move in flight. Fix a red rehearsal or a discovery miss where it is. Nothing is seeded from here; it goes back to the gateway, which re-asks. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-move.bpmn#Task_Drain . Draw the board of todos and beans candidate, extracted The todo board mounts inside the landing board, so harness cards and todo stickies share one surface. Each card carries an edit link only when the build composed one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/harness-default-rendering.bpmn#A_Board . Draw the sample candidate, extracted On a first translation: every diagram label, every persona and scenario string, and a seeded random fraction of the rest, with the seed written down so the sample can be drawn again. On a refresh: only the strings that were new or fuzzy. Hand the back-translator the msgstr values alone, keyed by an opaque id. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-round-trip.bpmn#Task_RT_Sample . Drop its positions and sweep orphans candidate, extracted Only after the content has moved: drop its positions from the layout layer and sweep any position whose note is now gone. Sweeping first would make the board authoritative over the folio for one step. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_UpdateLayer . Drop the file in the queue candidate, extracted Through the forge's upload form, a commit, or any other route that lands the file in the declared queue. The agent watches rather than chases: an arrival may be minutes or days away. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/content-acquisition.bpmn#P_Upload .

7352.title: Glossary: BPMN activities, E–Q
7352.content: Candidate terms extracted from every BPMN task and call activity: name as the label, its own <documentation> as the definition, the element id as the code. Each is the asset’s own text, verbatim and not curated, and carries the badge “candidate, extracted”. A person promotes one by authoring it. Authored terms are on their owning instance’s page, and those pages, the counts and the sources are linked from the glossary index. From: bootstrap 38 (SKOS) · bootstrap-tools 7 (SKOS) · cat-harness 393 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-core 70 (SKOS) · folio-assistant-sci 5 (SKOS). One of 3 pages of this type, split by the first letter of the label: all parts. Size: this page holds 163 terms and is 142 KB before compression, fetched in one request, within its budget of 1.0 MB. There is no search index: the filter below runs over this page, and the A–Z bar jumps within it. Already somebody else's concept? — check:term-mapping, bean 7wou | target | mapped | unmapped | undetermined | why undetermined | . | fhir | 0 | 897 | 0 | — | . | skos | 0 | 897 | 0 | — | . Undetermined is never “no match”. A vocabulary that could not be reached has said nothing, and the column above keeps that apart from a checked miss. The counts are reported and not graded: an unmapped candidate may be a term this corpus is right to coin. Per term. Every term on this page is unmapped on fhir, and unmapped on skos, unless its entry says otherwise. No entry says otherwise. Filter terms . 163 shown . E F G H I J K L M N O P Q

7353.title: E
7353.content: Edit it in place — it is your own content candidate, extracted The ordinary path, drawn so the process does not read as though every edit needs a copy. Content in a writable directory is authored content and is edited where it lives; the copy-out is for somebody else's bytes, not for yours. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/copy-out-materialized.bpmn#Task_EditDirectly . Edit the document in the row's pull request candidate, extracted One row, one branch, one active pull request: the agent edits on the row's branch and opens its pull request, or updates it when the row comes round again. A closed pull request the committee wants back is reopened, or replaced by a new one on the same branch; earlier ones stay listed in Agentic status. Agentic status (Green) says where it is, and Staging review opens the preview's what-changed page. Before the preview is staged, the agent writes the change set's Disposition (change set) on the Agent tab: one line per feedback item, starting from the people's Blue Disposition, after an optional Overall statement; the sheet shows it in Disposition (agent) and flags any item without a disposition, or one that differs from the people's. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_EditInPullRequest . Edit the flagged passage and re-inject candidate, extracted The reviewer corrects the passage in the PO rather than sending the whole translation back. Flows to Task_PoInject, so the round-trip QA runs again over the corrected text — "edit the translation and re-run QA", which is what the adjudication step has always offered and what this process could not do. A userTask, not a service task: this is the one step here where a person edits content, and the lane's actor is the reviewer who just adjudicated. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-workflow.bpmn#Task_EditTranslation . Edit, comment or raise todos on the folio's copy candidate, extracted The copied asset is now writable content of the target folio with recorded upstream provenance (KgAsset.source). The folio author may edit it in place, attach review comments, or raise todos (todo-manager) against it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/copy-into-folio.bpmn#Task_WorkOnCopy . Ensure the tracking label exists candidate, extracted Create the tracking label (the label input) with --force so it exists before either issue path runs — the close path filters on it too, and on a repository that has never had a finding it would not exist yet. Filter the corpus, choose the granularity, decompose the question candidate, extracted The paper's Planner. Three outputs, and the middle one is the method's substance: a filtered document subset, the granularity to search at, and the sub-questions. CHOOSING THE GRANULARITY PER QUESTION is the whole point of parsing at several. A broad question is answered from summaries and a specific one from chunks; a pipeline that picks once has answered every future question the same way. This checkout cannot yet offer the choice — l1-blocks.ts produces blocks, there is no summary level — so this step SAYS which granularity it searched rather than implying the corpus offered alternatives. Re-entered on every iteration, not only the first: the sub-questions are re-derived from what has been found so far, which is what makes the loop a search rather than a retry. 7355.title: G
7355.content: Gate every slice: slice:sqlite:check candidate, extracted For every slice: build twice and require one sha256; read the row digest back from the file and require it to equal the digest computed from the source without SQLite; run an FTS5 phrase query for a known row; and audit the payloads with auditPayloadTree (deploy payloads as written, the kg slice's pointers against the committed payload tree). A slice whose rows do not match its source fails; it never passes as whole. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/slice-sqlite-publish.bpmn#A_Check . Give a link, a description, or neither candidate, extracted "Or neither" is a real outcome, not a failure. The ask says what happens if nothing comes, and then that happens — the work proceeds without the resource and says so. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/content-acquisition.bpmn#P_Respond . Grant a dispensation, with its reason candidate, extracted The rule applies and this subject is a stated exception. A kind: "human" entry with result: "pass" overrides the script's fail for that criterion, and ONLY while its field_hash matches the current source — so the dispensation is scoped to the version it was granted against, lapses when the block changes, and never becomes precedent. There is nothing to overturn later; the source moving overturns it. A dispensation with no notes is not a dispensation. It is an override somebody applied to get to green, and nobody can review it afterwards — which is why this step is not relaxable. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/criterion-adjudication.bpmn#A_Dispensation . 7356.content: Hand back to the discussion candidate, extracted The composed question goes, unchanged, to the discussion agent, which asks it through this same process on its yes branch and routes the answer back: the sibling's half of Process_HandBackToDiscussion (a task here, not a call, because that process calls this one). The sibling also shows it in its own thread, never only there. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/ask-the-person.bpmn#A_HandBack . Then keep working on the recommended option where it can be undone, or stop if blocking. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#S_HandBack . Hand new feedback to the row's agent; take over stalled rows candidate, extracted On every poll, changed or not, new Blue feedback goes verbatim to the agent working the row, and a stalled row is restarted or taken over. For each row: new Blue feedback goes, verbatim and in the same poll, to the thread that owns the row (named in its Agent row or Feedback (agent)), and Feedback (agent) says who has it. A row is stalled when its Blue cells changed, or Ready for agent turned Yes, more than 10 minutes ago and no Agent step was recorded since; or when its agent recorded no step for 2 hours. A stalled row's owning thread is asked once; with no answer within 10 minutes, or a thread that is done or stopped, the watcher takes the row over, or asks the coordinator for a new thread, and writes the new owner, the step and a link into Feedback (agent). BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/review-log-watch.bpmn#Task_StallCheck . SWOT does not make that selection and does not make the decision. What is handed over includes the ambiguities from A_RecordAmbiguous and the fact that the candidates are UNRANKED. A receiving methodology that assumed an ordered list would be reading a priority SWOT never established. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_HandOff . BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#E_HumanEyes .

7358.title: J
7358.content: Judge the assets in their design candidate, extracted A person looks at the ingested assets laid out in the design they are for, at BOTH a web and a mobile width. THIS IS A HUMAN STEP INSIDE INGESTION, stated rather than hidden: ingestion of a THEME SOURCE is attended at this step, while ingestion of everything else never reaches it. A judgement made at one viewport is incomplete, not passed, and the wireframe of the surface (wireframe-design-review) says what each layout was meant to be. A clean build, a passing suite and every gate can all miss what only rendering the page and looking finds. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#R_Judge .

7359.title: K
7359.content: Keep it as a trial: the unpublished trashcan candidate, extracted A trial goes to the kept trashcan: addressable, exported, never published. Its node declares $schema: folio-fsh-guts/v1 and carries the bean or issue it was written under, since it was never moved from anywhere and a movedFrom would be invented provenance. It is NOT refreshed: a trial records what the source looked like when it was tried. Promoting a trial means running this process again with permanent = yes, so the gates are asked afresh. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Trial . Keep the edit, re-pin candidate, extracted The local edit wins, so nothing is re-materialized — and the pin moves to the upstream revision that was compared against. Re-pinning is the half that is easy to forget and is the reason this is a step rather than an absence: without it the same upstream change is detected as new on every cycle, and a contributor is asked the same settled question for ever. The record says the copy is deliberately divergent FROM a named revision, which is a different claim from being stale against an unknown one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/refresh-materialized.bpmn#Task_KeepLocal .

7360.title: L
7360.content: Land it in library/ candidate, extracted A permanent sample joins the library as an L1 source, with the materialization record (purpose, gates, fixity) beside it. From here refresh-materialized governs it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/sample-import.bpmn#Task_Library . Land the bytes in the copier's own folio/ candidate, extracted Into the copier's own declared folio/, never a scratch area — a directory nobody declared is a directory nobody gates, and the copy would be publishable by accident. The copy is NOT read-only: it is the copier's own content, makes no claim about anybody else's bytes, and freezing it too would mean the next person needs a copy of the copy. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/copy-out-materialized.bpmn#Task_Land . Land the feature's PRs candidate, extracted Phase 6's "explicit confirmation before merging to main", made a step that can refuse. Once per pull request the feature still has open, after the sign-off is recorded and before the issue is closed: an issue is not closed on a feature that is not on main. merge-to-main.bpmn reads each head's evidence live, establishes that the owner authorised THAT merge (a stakeholder sign-off or the BA's confirmation is acceptance of the feature, not authorisation to merge it, unless the owner's own words say so), records the authorisation, merges, and confirms the base. A PR the owner holds or refuses stays open, and A_Close then waits: the BA's authorisation to close does not cover a feature that did not land. An increment the owner asked to land earlier in Phase 6 went through the same sub-process at that time. Where cat-harness.sdlc is switched on, this step is the opt-in process merge-to-main (Process_MergeToMain, sdlc/processes/merge-to-main.bpmn); it is not called from here, because a layer without that sub-graph does not have it (owner card Q-OPTIN-CALLS A, 2026-11-12). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-close.bpmn#Call_MergeToMain . New UI is where untranslated strings enter, because nothing was stale — there was nothing there before. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/theme-ui-review.bpmn#A_Locales . Lay out the options, with what each costs candidate, extracted Every option the agent could narrow the question to, each with what it costs and what it makes hard to undo. Narrow from context first: an option the agent could have ruled out itself wastes the reader's attention. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/human-agent-discussion.bpmn#A_LayOutOptions . Leave a reachable way back candidate, extracted Leave the way back reachable: the collapsed window becomes a control in its own position and focus moves to it — left alone, focus lands on <body> and the keyboard position is lost. An action whose inverse is not reachable is not a toggle. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-open-close.bpmn#A_OfferWayBack . Leave it as feedback candidate, extracted With no write tool the reader's point is not lost: it is recorded as feedback for someone who can write. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/harness-default-rendering.bpmn#A_Todo . Leave it referenced, record why candidate, extracted A refusal is not a failure of the process — it is the process working. The node stays referenced, which means the graph still knows it exists and where, and the refusing gate's basis is recorded so the next caller does not re-litigate it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/materialize-remote.bpmn#Task_StayRef . Leave the content exactly where it is candidate, extracted The reader said no: nothing moves, no position is dropped, and the board is left exactly as it was. Drawn as its own end state because a destructive action whose refusal is not drawn gets performed by accident. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_Cancel . Link L1 nodes into the corpus graph candidate, extracted Anything in library/ is L1 source content. A knowledge-graph reference from any artefact -- paper, L2, L3 -- resolves to it through library/. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-build-l1-kg.bpmn#Task_Link . Link the work to an issue candidate, extracted Feature work must be linked to a GitHub issue. Scan before creating, and never create one without the BA's permission — an issue is the stakeholder's record, not the agent's scratchpad. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Issue . Link to existing issue candidate, extracted A match was found: ask the person whether the requirements go on #NNN, then link the work there. The issue is where stakeholders sign off, so no phase proceeds without one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-issue-linking.bpmn#A_LinkIssue . List the harnesses this could be candidate, extracted Zero or more. The candidate everybody has is bootstrap itself. Context may name others: "please set up <owner>/<repo> here" names one, and so does any Harness built on bootstrap that the Requestor mentions. This step narrows; it does not decide. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_ListHarnesses . List the locations this could install to candidate, extracted Zero or more. Is this a git repository already, or were one or more URLs to repositories supplied? Both are Knowledge Graph Data Stores; the difference is only how they are reached. A location whose root already holds a declaration, <name>.json, is not a blank slate, and says so in the question. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/discussion.bpmn#A_ListLocations . List the steps the declarations name candidate, extracted In the order of the table in initialization-steps: declaration, needs, each dependency's instructions, the documents at their IRIs (checked above; the report leads with them), directories, assets, README, README sections, site. Each step names the declaration that names it, so a reader can see why it is there. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/complete-initialization.bpmn#A_ListSteps . Load the active voices candidate, extracted The activated set only, never everything shipped. An id naming no shipped voice is an error rather than a skip — a folio that believes it is applying a voice and is applying nothing has the cleanest-looking output of the three. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_LoadActive . Log the failure candidate, extracted Every failure path passes through here, so "logged as failed" is a step somebody performs rather than an adjective on an end event. What differs between the ways in is the message, which is an input, not the mechanism. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_LogFailure . Log the start of the install candidate, extracted REQUIRED logging, which is what drawing the call says. Logged before anything is written, so an install interrupted halfway is distinguishable from one never begun. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_LogInstallStart .

7361.title: M
7361.content: Make sure every step is done candidate, extracted Following a harness's instructions once is not the same as every step being done. complete-initialization walks the steps the declarations name — FIRST the harness's JSON Schemas and JSON-LD at the IRIs they name, the primary step of initializing a Knowledge Graph harness; then declared directories, assets, the README and its sections, and the site that carries the documents — checks each, does what can be done, asks the person for what only they can do, and reports every step in its state. An agent may be dispatched to run it on its own: it needs nothing but that diagram and the declarations. BPMN activities of bootstrap · source bootstrap/processes/initialize-harness.bpmn#A_CompleteInitialization . Make sure gh-pages exists and Pages serves it candidate, extracted Provisioning the target, owned by this process rather than by the publication step that calls it. Pages cannot serve a branch that does not exist, so in order: (1) an orphan gh-pages branch exists — git ls-remote --heads origin gh-pages; if absent, push a placeholder (index.html + .nojekyll); (2) Pages is on, Source = the gh-pages branch at / — gh api -X POST repos/<o>/<r>/pages -f source[branch]=gh-pages -f source[path]=/ when gh is signed in, otherwise the exact manual step (Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → gh-pages, / (root)). Each half is done, not done, or could not be determined; never assumed. BPMN activities of bootstrap-tools · source bootstrap-tools/processes/render-kg-to-github-pages.bpmn#A_Provision . Map values onto palette roles candidate, extracted surface / ink / edge / accent, shared across every kind. A palette per kind would be three spellings of "accent colour", free to disagree about what an accent IS. Where the source is SILENT on a role, say so and mark the value a choice rather than dressing an invention as a measurement. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/ingest-theme.bpmn#Task_MapRoles . Mark every copy answered candidate, extracted Chat copies keep their text: the question struck through and "[Edit: <letter> chosen by <who>, <time>]" added. Cards closed with the chosen option. The sheet's "Decision needed" block replaced by the decision and who made it. Withdrawn or superseded hand-backs marked the same way, with the reason. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#D_MarkAnswered . Materialise the part candidate, extracted The ONLY way bytes arrive. Purpose first, then the five gates — size, restrictions, copyright, retention, source loss — then fetch with fixity, or stay referenced with the refusing gate's basis recorded. Both ends of that subprocess return here and the walk continues: one part refused is not the subscription refused. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Call_Materialize . Materialize remote content (the five gates) candidate, extracted The shared subprocess. It resolves the request against the source descriptor, then asks size, restrictions, copyright, retention and source loss, and either fetches with fixity or leaves the content referenced. This process does not restate any of that; it waits for the outcome. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/sample-import.bpmn#Call_Materialize . Measure the cutover: separation:cutover:check candidate, extracted Run bun run cat separation:cutover:check --site in the SEPARATED repository (Tool separation-cutover-check). Six conditions, each decided by an existing gate and none assumed: every declared layer mounted at its pin; every path a declaration names resolves (check:declaration-resolution — directories, assets, visualisers, needs); no wiring still names the monorepo (livesAt, a submodule, a reusable workflow, a path into the old checkout); no import or reference against the layer order; and the site builds from the mounts alone. A finding inside a mounted layer is upstream's and is listed, not counted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-cutover.bpmn#Task_CutoverCheck . Measure the signals candidate, extracted Files and bytes per layer, clone cost (bun run cat health), gate time, merge contention, the candidate's cohesion and cut (kg:detangle), wrong-direction edges, and the would-be tools package's import cone. Recorded in the work context; none alone is a trigger. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Task_Measure . Mechanical checks, both viewports candidate, extracted Tool wireframe-check renders every candidate at a web and a mobile viewport. It fails on horizontal overflow at mobile width, on placeholder text, and on a missing viewport, and writes screenshots and a script entry per criterion. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn#D_Check . Merge into each locale candidate, extracted Merge each refreshed template into every locale's catalogue: new strings arrive empty, changed ones fuzzy, and obsolete ones are kept as #~ entries, never deleted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_MergeLocales . Merge the one source PR to main candidate, extracted All the templates in one PR to main, merged before any locale starts, so every translator branches from the same main. Once it has merged, its branch receives nothing more: a later fix to the source is a new PR. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_SourcePR . Merge the PR candidate, extracted Merge the layer's PR to main, then confirm the template checks pass on main. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-refresh.bpmn#Task_TR_Merge . Merge the pull request candidate, extracted The agent merges the row's pull request, and Agentic status says merged. The change set's Dispositions blurb, as it stands when Ready for merge is set to Yes, is the summary: it goes into the merge, and closes the change set's issue. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/content/contributor-feedback.bpmn#Task_Merge . Mirror it to the feedback channel candidate, extracted Review sheet: the "Decision needed" block in the row's agent column, Agentic status Needs you (the document layer's review-sheet-script skill). Issue or PR: a comment. An extra copy, never instead of the discussion. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/hand-back-to-discussion.bpmn#S_Mirror . Mount each layer at its declared path candidate, extracted Sparse checkout of the declaration and the chosen directories, copied to the mount path (by default the layer's home path, so relative imports and sibling discovery hold). Never onto tracked bytes; never onto a directory no lock says this mount made; never over edits to a previous mount — those are left untouched and reported. A replay of the lock tries the index's layers cache ref first (refs/cat/layers/<key>, then refs/cat/layers/main): one shallow fetch, every byte verified against the lock, and any layer that does not verify is fetched from its own repository. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-dependency.bpmn#Task_MountInstances . Mount the branch tip at the declared path candidate, extracted A branch source keyed by tip: branch-store mount --id <dir-id> writes the tip's files at the declared path, so every reader finds the directory where it always was; push splices edits back onto the tip, never forcing, and a same-file race is a conflict. The branch's NAME is the declaring directory's storage (or source) — a branch no declaration names is refused rather than guessed. A commit-keyed branch is read per commit through its own store (qa-store), not mounted. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_MountBranchTip . Mount the Lean branch store candidate, extracted bun run cat state:mount (or branch-store.ts mount --id <id>) at the start of the site build, as for beans/: puts the branch tip on disk at the declared path. Reads the RENDER; writes nothing to the branch. A site build of a folio whose Lean did not change starts here. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-sci · source folio-assistant-sci/processes/content/lean-docs-publish.bpmn#Task_Mount . Mount the remote tree at its pin candidate, extracted A remote source: another repository's tree at a full 40-character commit. bun run cat mount:remote lays it down at the declared path and locks its tree digest; it is never written back, because the bytes are somebody else's at somebody else's pin. Usually reached through a source.remote layer in the root index.config.json (legacy: remoteMounts), which expands a whole harness and its closure — Process_MountDependency. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/mount-subgraph.bpmn#Task_MountRemotePin . Move harness output about it to the host candidate, extracted QA verdicts, translation templates, the exported graph and the glossary ledger are harness output ABOUT the graph: they live with the harness (kgQaHomeFor, translationsHomeFor). The content keeps only what its own checks need; the leak test's pending list is empty. The one exception is a separated layer that declares a qa directory of its own with storage: its verdicts are its own repository's, published to that repository's qa-reports branch (step 10), and read by a host at the commit it pins. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-prepare.bpmn#Task_Hosted . Move it into its repositories candidate, extracted Create the repositories, drain, seed, consume additively, release, and check every identifier dereferences. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation.bpmn#Call_Move . Move it into its repository candidate, extracted Create the repository, drain, copy the staged contents in, re-point the declaration, verify a fresh clone, then consume, release and check every identifier dereferences. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/sub-kg-lifecycle.bpmn#Call_Move . Move the entry's ref and re-cache the declaration candidate, extracted Only after every held part has been through the refresh. Moving the ref first would make the records of parts not yet refreshed describe a commit the entry no longer names. The cached declaration is replaced so the review that follows shows what the NEW pin offers, including subgraphs that did not exist at the old one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_RePin .

7362.title: N
7362.content: Name the subject and the level candidate, extracted One sentence naming WHAT is being analysed and at WHICH level — individual, organisational, national, international. The source requires this before anything is listed: "the classification of a variable also depends on the purpose of the practice", and the criteria for assigning a variable to a quadrant "may be more difficult to clarify if the methodology is not used for a company but for a country". It also bounds the known limitation that SWOT "is rarely deployed at lower than the organization level", where one scan drives strategy for units its factors do not hold equally for. Naming the level does not remove that risk; it makes it visible in the record. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/swot-analysis.bpmn#A_FrameSubject . Name the substrate, pin a full commit SHA candidate, extracted owner/repo and a 40-character commit SHA — never a branch, never an abbreviated SHA. The schema refuses anything else (SubscriptionSchema.ref), and this step exists so the refusal is met while choosing rather than at commit time. A tag replaces the SHA only once the substrate publishes releases. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/subscribe-kg.bpmn#Task_Pin . Name what will move, and where it lands candidate, extracted Before anything moves, name the content that would move — what it is, with its size and age — and where it lands. The confirmation sits in front of the move: an agent never relocates a durable artefact on its own initiative. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/ui/board-relocate.bpmn#A_AskConfirm . Narrative description per image, localized candidate, extracted Applies equally to an image EXTRACTED FROM A PDF (Task_FiguresTables), not only to an uploaded one. An agent opens every image and vector render and records a verdict in the library's image-verdicts.json: role (figure, logo or decorative), the reason, and a draft description in English plus ar, zh, es, fr and ru, which the apply-image-verdicts.ts arm lays over images.json on every ingest. Images judged figure are kept as WebP, quality 80, at most 1600 px; logos, decorative fragments and page scans are not. Every description stays a draft until a person confirms it with bun run cat narratives. Method: skill document-intake, "Figures and captioned tables: describe, keep, transcribe". BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-derive-content.bpmn#Task_Image . Narrative review candidate, extracted Descend into Process_NarrativeReview. The actor takes on the narrative-reviewer lane for this call path only. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/review-task.bpmn#Call_NarrativeReview .

7363.title: O
7363.content: OCR to ocr/page-*.txt candidate, extracted Each page is read in the document's languages (--lang-hint, from dc.language.iso), narrowed to the script the page shows. A page Tesseract is unsure of (mean word confidence under 70) is read again with each other installed script added, and the most confident read is kept: a French article's Arabic abstract, or the Latin URLs in an Arabic document's references. A document ingested this way keeps its text in ocr/ and only a stub in sections/, which the documented sections/ grep cannot see. That asymmetry is why the corpus-grep checklist has a fourth tier. The run also records WHICH SOFTWARE made the pages, in ocr/run-context.json: a folio-run-context/v1 (cat-harness schemas/run-context.ts, the record test runs and QA reports use for the same question), naming the OCR engine, the rasteriser and each language model with its version and the sha256 of the bytes that ran. Two OCRs of one scan can read differently ("Manual" and "Manval"), and without it neither could be told from the other or reproduced. BPMN activities of folio-assistant-core · source folio-assistant-core/processes/library/ingest-extract-structure.bpmn#Task_Ocr . Offer KG destinations for the agreed set candidate, extracted Without this step, agreed and signed-off requirements exist only as an issue and a conversation, and the knowledge graph never learns them. ONE question for the SET, not one per requirement: a six-phase run can agree many, and asking six times is the same failure as a form that re-asks what it was already told. The options are DERIVED from the graphs this layer declares in <name>.json, read at the time of asking, so a layer that adds a graph gets it in the offer without anybody editing a skill. Never a list typed from memory. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_OfferKg . Open a block's 🌐 translation pane candidate, extracted On every page, source-language pages included, a block's 📣 panel has a 🌐 pane that lists every locale's current translation of the block, its status, and how it came to be (chosen.how, chosen.by). On a translated page its own locale comes first and the others are collapsed. ✎ Fix translation opens, per locale, each of the block's strings with its candidates ranked as the auto-pick ranks them: the text; the source's kind, id and version; who proposed it, linked to the issue it came from; the date; its QA results; a stale mark when it was made for another source text; whether an official source's English matched exactly; and which one is the default. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-review-adjudication.bpmn#Task_TRA_BlockPane . Open a ready PR and comment candidate, extracted Commit on translation-adjudication/issue-<n>, authored by the issue's author, open a ready pull request that names the issue, and comment the summary on the issue: what was recorded and what was refused. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/translation-review-adjudication.bpmn#Task_TRA_OpenPR . Open or close a role to an actor candidate, extracted The join every other diagram depends on. An empty roles is a DETERMINED empty — it says the actor takes on none — and is not the same as an absent one, which asserts nothing. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/actor-role-administration.bpmn#Task_AssignRoles . Open or EDIT the one tracking issue candidate, extracted Findings: EDIT the one open issue carrying the tracking label (the label input) if there is one, otherwise create it, with the report as the body. One issue edited in place, never a new issue or a comment per run, so the tracking issue never becomes a feed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/global-tasks.bpmn#GT_TrackIssue . Open the locale PR to main candidate, extracted One PR per locale, based on and targeting main. Never into the source branch. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/library/processes/multi-locale-translation.bpmn#Task_ML_LocalePR . Open the rule's citation candidate, extracted Every rule resolves to a real library/ section or a KG node, and carries the quote it was read from. Opening it is what lets a reviewer say WHY the rule applies — and it is the only way to catch a rule that misread its own source. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/content/voice-review.bpmn#Task_OpenCitation . Open the session record candidate, extracted Writes id, actor and startedAt, with open and claimed empty. An empty open is the NORMAL state, not an unfinished one: an agent reading, answering or deciding is in no process at all. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/session-state-machine.bpmn#A_OpenSession . Options analysis how to implement candidate, extracted On the single edge from Start_Process_CRDM_Deliver into A_Implement, so the approach is chosen before any code exists. By Phase 6 the needs, requirements and data model are signed off, which is exactly the evidence an options analysis needs and the reason it belongs here rather than earlier: at Call_Needs there is nothing to weigh, and after A_Implement the choice has been made in code. The three loop-backs into A_Implement — _5 (increment rejected), _7 (MVP not ready), _13 (feedback translated) — deliberately BYPASS this call. Routing them through it would run the subprocess on every iteration of the inner loop, which is the ceremony this design refuses: a gate invoked on every pass stops being read. An iteration reworks an approach already chosen; if the APPROACH is what is wrong, that is not a loop iteration and it belongs to the calling step in crdm-requirements.bpmn. Contrast upstream-version-adoption, where the loop DOES re-enter the analysis. There the loop-back returns to A_Impact, which re-gathers the evidence, so the second pass weighs genuinely different inputs. Here the loop returns to implementation with the evidence unchanged. A_Implement carries a note on the bean (its claim is the OPEN that Process_CRDM calls first); this step carries no bean op, because Process_OptionsAnalysis ends with its own decision-audit note on the bean the caller claimed. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#Call_OptionsAnalysis .

7364.title: P
7364.content: Package with digests candidate, extracted The serialization alone is not a package. A package is an addressable set — the JSON-LD, the assets it references, and a manifest naming every file with its digest and byte count. The manifest is what makes a REMOVED file detectable, which a per-file signature cannot do on its own. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-to-portal.bpmn#A_Package . Parent consumes, additively candidate, extracted The parent pins the pair (a commit while staging, a version once released) — a code dependency as a source.remote instance in its root index.config.json (remote-mount skill), never a submodule — repoints its imports, and keeps its own copy until it is green with the dependency declared. Where cat-harness.sdlc is switched on, this step is the opt-in process upstream-version-adoption (Process_UpstreamAdoption, sdlc/processes/upstream-version-adoption.bpmn); it is not called from here, because a layer without that sub-graph does not have it (owner card Q-OPTIN-CALLS A, 2026-11-12). BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/kg/kg-separation-move.bpmn#Task_Consume . Phase 1 Needs candidate, extracted Identify the stakeholders, synthesise a needs statement from the sources, and loop until the BA and the stakeholders both recognise it. The loop is the phase: a needs statement nobody confirmed is an agent's summary, not a requirement. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Needs . Phase 1: Identify stakeholders candidate, extracted The agent asks the BA who is affected by this change. The BA knows the domain — the agent does not guess. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#A_Stakeholders . Phase 1: Synthesise needs from sources candidate, extracted From the chat, issue, uploads and library sources, write a clear, jargon-free statement of what is needed and why, tied to a concrete workflow. Post it on the GitHub issue, not in chat, and ask the requester and stakeholders to review it. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-needs.bpmn#A_Synthesise . Phase 2: Map current workflow (BPA) candidate, extracted Business-process analysis here means reading the existing diagrams under processes/ and drawing the gap, so the skill that implements this step is the BPMN one. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#A_MapWorkflow . Phase 4a: Compare the viable options candidate, extracted Phase 4 often ends with a CHOICE rather than a plan, and this is the step that hands it over. Per option: what it does, its pro, its con, what it changes DOWNSTREAM, and how reversible it is — laid out where the rows can be read against each other, then one recommendation and a stated default. A step of its own rather than a line inside A_DefineReqs, because it has a different output and a different reader: the impact analysis is for the record, the comparison is the thing the BA answers from. Folding it in is how it gets skipped — the analysis feels finished, so the options go over as a list of names. When Call_Wireframe ran, its wireframe candidates are among the options: one row per candidate, with a link to its web and mobile screenshots. Skipped legitimately when the analysis yields ONE viable approach. Do not manufacture alternatives to fill a table. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#A_CompareOptions . Phase 5 Plan + sign-off candidate, extracted The approved requirements become work-plan items, the BA signs off, and the branch is announced on the issue. The announcement is on the single edge into delivery, so the three loops back into implementation do not re-announce. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Signoff . Phase 5: Create beans candidate, extracted The agent mints the implementation beans itself with beans create, running the exact-title existence check first. The engine has no create op — it claims, notes and resolves the instance's OWN bean — so what this step records here is a note that the plan now exists. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-signoff.bpmn#A_CreateBeans . Phase 6 Implement + acceptance candidate, extracted One phase and not three, because the loops say so: an increment the BA rejects, an MVP that is not ready, and stakeholder findings all route back into implementation. A subprocess has one exit and cannot be re-entered once finished, so splitting this region would have changed what the diagram says. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Deliver . Phase 6: Implement (feature branch + PR) candidate, extracted Inner loop: agent claims a bean, implements on feature branch, opens PR, posts summary to the issue. When the requirement changes a rendered surface, implement against the wireframe candidate the requester or BA chose in Phases 3–4 (Process_WireframeDesignReview, called from Process_CRDM_Requirements), not against a fresh design; and the delivery summary links the chosen candidate beside the after-screenshot, so the reviewer can see the build matches what was approved. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-deliver.bpmn#A_Implement . Phases 2–4 BPA + requirements candidate, extracted Map the current workflow, then define the requirements and the impact they carry, and loop until approved. Same shape as Phase 1 and for the same reason: an unapproved requirement is a proposal. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements.bpmn#Call_Requirements . Phases 3–4: Define requirements + impact candidate, extracted Two skills, because this step is two things: the requirements come from the CRDM process, the impact half is a question about the entities and relations the change touches, which is what data modelling answers; a folio-content skill such as content-graph is not one this harness diagram can bind. BPMN activities of cat-harness · source cat-harness/processes/process/crdm-requirements-definition.bpmn#A_DefineReqs . The basic flow's ACCEPT step: choosing an arrival route, writing the bytes into the declared queue of the layer that will own them, and discharging what that route does not discharge for you. The routes, what each writer owes, and the two that are mechanisms against the one that is a persona are in the upload-routes skill; upload-url composes the forge URL for the web route from the declaration rather than from a literal, because a hand-written one can 404. A userTask asserts a human performs it, and this lane is "Contributor (human or agent)" because both do; asserting human-only would be an activity-fulfilment-kind contradiction. A plain task asserts nothing about the performer. WHY THE BEAN OP IS note AND NOT claim. Placing a file claims nothing; it adds to a queue. What it owes the work plan is visibility. 7365.title: Q
7365.content: QA gate: check dispositions and PR candidate, extracted Reads: the change set's Disposition (change set), the people's Blue Disposition and feedback, the pull request's diff at its head commit, and the staging QA report. Checks that every feedback item has one disposition; that each agrees with the people's Blue Disposition; that each Accepted or Partially accepted item has the change in the diff, and a Not accepted, Noted, Duplicate or Out of scope item has none; that the diff changes nothing no disposition accounts for; and that the QA report for the staged commit has no failing gate. Writes: QA gate (change set) on the Agent tab, first line "Passed <head sha>: …" or "Failed <head sha>: <why>", and QA report (change set), the report's link. The sheet shows the gate under Staging review; a pass for an older commit reads as stale. It ends with Record agent step (record-agent-step.bpmn): the Agent tab row first, then Feedback (agent) from it, then the sheet read back, never Feedback (agent) alone. 7378.title: Términos redactados
7378.content: Bootstrap terms . | término | etiquetas alternativas | definición | . | Nodo (Node) | — | Un archivo, o una parte de un archivo direccionable mediante un fragmento de IRI, nombrado por un IRI. | . | Referencia (Reference) | — | La designación que un Nodo hace de otro Nodo por su IRI. | . | Esquema de nodo (Node Schema) | — | Un esquema contra el que se puede validar un Nodo: un JSON Schema, o un esquema externo publicado como el de BPMN. | . | Tipo de nodo (Node Kind) | — | Un nombre emparejado con un Esquema de nodo. | . | Subtipo (Subkind) | — | Un Tipo de nodo cuyo Esquema de nodo exige todo lo que exige el de otro Tipo de nodo, de modo que todo Nodo que lo satisface satisface también el otro. | . | Instancia de nodo (Node Instance) | — | Un Nodo que nombra su Tipo de nodo, en $schema o en el preámbulo, y satisface el Esquema de nodo de ese tipo. | . | Tipo de grafo (Graph Typology) | — | Un conjunto con nombre de Tipos de nodo. | . | Declaración (Declaration) | — | Un documento JSON, <name>.json, que da un nombre y enumera entradas de directorio y entradas de archivo. | . | Extensión (Extension) | — | Un campo de una Declaración, o de una de sus entradas, que no se define aquí. Un lector que no reconoce el campo lo ignora, y el resto de la Declaración conserva su significado. | . | Subgrafo (Subgraph) | — | Una entrada de directorio de una Declaración: un id, un directorio y los Tipos de grafo a los que pertenecen los tipos de sus Instancias de nodo. | . | Recurso (Asset) | — | Una entrada de archivo de una Declaración: un archivo sobre el propio repositorio, cuyo campo role indica para qué sirve. | . | Grafo de conocimiento (Knowledge Graph) | — | Los Esquemas de nodo, las Instancias de nodo y los Recursos que enumera una Declaración, en una versión dada del repositorio. Publicadas como JSON-LD, las afirmaciones de las Instancias de nodo de cada Subgrafo forman un grafo con nombre. | . | Dependencia (Dependency) | — | Una entrada needs de una Declaración que nombra otro Grafo de conocimiento. Las Referencias pueden apuntar desde las Instancias de nodo de este grafo hacia el nombrado, nunca en sentido inverso. | . | Contenido (Content) | — | Instancias de nodo que describen el objeto de un Grafo de conocimiento, como registros, documentos, catálogos y sus términos, y no cómo trabajar con él. | . | Tarea (Task) | — | Una unidad de trabajo, expresada por lo que necesita para comenzar y lo que produce. | . | Actor | — | Una persona, un agente o un programa que puede llevar a cabo Tareas. | . | Habilidad (Skill) | — | A Node Instance stating a responsibility an Actor carries out to complete a Task: as natural-language instructions to follow, as a contract to be tested against, or both.
