8431.title: Invocation
8431.content: The user’s request maps to one of three modes; pick the right one without asking: . | user phrase | mode | how | . | “watch main” / “watch upstream” / no target | branch:main | poll origin/main every 5 min | . | “watch PR 516” / “watch the PR” / “watch this PR” | pr:N | mcp__github__subscribe_pr_activity (event-driven) | . | “watch branch foo/bar” / “watch claude/x-y” | branch:foo/bar | poll origin/foo/bar every 5 min | . | “watch foo/bar PR 42” | pr:42 + maybe branch | subscribe + poll | . If ambiguous, default to branch:main.

8432.title: 1.  Stash the baseline
8432.content: Before arming anything, record the current state so the §3 review compares cleanly: . git fetch origin <BRANCH> 2>/dev/null # Sanitize branch name for use in a file path: replace `/` with `_` # (e.g. `feature/foo` → `feature_foo`). Without this, branches with # slashes silently land in non-existent directory trees. SAFE_BRANCH=$(printf '%s' "<BRANCH>" | tr '/' '_') git rev-parse "origin/<BRANCH>" > "/tmp/_watch_baseline_${SAFE_BRANCH}.sha" . For PR mode, instead capture the latest PR head SHA: . mcp__github__pull_request_read(method="get", pullNumber=N, owner=..., repo=...) # stash result["head"]["sha"] .

8433.title: 2.  Arm the watcher
8433.content: Branch mode — Monitor with poll loop . Use the Monitor tool, persistent: true, 5-minute poll: . Monitor: description: "origin/<BRANCH> new commits" persistent: true command: | BRANCH="<BRANCH>" last=$(git ls-remote origin "$BRANCH" | cut -f1) while true; do cur=$(git ls-remote origin "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null | cut -f1) if [ -n "$cur" ] && [ "$cur" != "$last" ]; then git fetch origin "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null # one line per new commit, oldest first git log --reverse --oneline "$last..$cur" | head -20 last=$cur fi sleep 300 done . Each new commit becomes one notification line. PR mode — GitHub MCP subscription . Use mcp__github__subscribe_pr_activity directly. Already event-driven — no polling needed. The harness delivers <github-webhook-activity> events for comments, CI status, reviews, and merges. See the existing PR-subscription guidance in the system prompt for handling.

8434.title: 3.  Per-event integration checklist
8434.content: For every notification (branch commit or PR event), run through these four questions in order — stop at the first “no” or “no action”: . Q1 — Should we integrate? . | Is the change on a file we touch in this branch? Quick check: git diff --name-only HEAD <NEW_SHA> -- $(git diff --name-only $(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)..HEAD). | If yes and the change is small, rebase / pull now. | If yes but large, defer until the immediate task ships and add a TODO. | If no overlap, skip Q2/Q3/Q4 and acknowledge with a one-liner. | . Q2 — Does it conflict? . | Try a dry rebase in a fresh worktree. Use mktemp -d so the path is unique (avoids collisions with previous failed runs and with parallel /watch invocations) and clean up unconditionally via trap: . PROBE=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rebase-probe.XXXXXX) trap 'git worktree remove --force "$PROBE" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$PROBE"' EXIT git worktree add "$PROBE" HEAD >/dev/null ( cd "$PROBE" && git rebase "origin/<BRANCH>" ) status=$? # trap fires on EXIT . | Conflicts (status != 0) → first attempt auto-resolve for the recurring drift-conflict pattern (see §2a below); only flag the user if auto-resolve fails or the conflict is non-trivial (overlapping logic edits, schema rewrites, etc.). | . §2a — Auto-resolve drift-conflict pattern (qou-v0t8: Contended Tree-Measuring Audit Witnesses) . 🛑 qou-v0t8 RULE (OVERRIDES OLD REGEN-ON-BRANCH ADVICE): Tree-measuring audit witnesses count properties across the whole working tree and are regenerated on main’s own cadence. NEVER regenerate or commit any of the contended tree-measuring audit witnesses from a feature branch — doing so either walks a drain-only ratchet backwards (if behind main) or immediately re-acquires a merge conflict on the next main landing: . | computations/audits/q0-anchor-consistency-audit.witness.json | computations/mpf-float-source-audit.witness.json | computations/mpf-import-time-dps-audit.witness.json | computations/never-raises-dps-audit.witness.json | computations/witness-float64-padding-audit.witness.json | computations/witness-raw-float64-audit.witness.json | computations/q0-value-drift-audit.witness.json | computations/no-free-parameter-certificate.witness.json | computations/codata-truncation-audit.witness.json (plus witness-value-copy-audit, compute-audit-scan, derivation-chain-audit, e0-calibration-audit) | . The recipe when git rebase origin/<BRANCH> halts on any contended audit witness (run on the real branch, not the probe worktree): . # 1. If the conflicting commit ONLY touched contended audit witnesses, drop/skip it: git diff --name-only --cached | grep -qE '\.witness\.json$' && \ ! git diff --name-only --cached | grep -vE '(q0-anchor-consistency-audit|mpf-float-source-audit|mpf-import-time-dps-audit|never-raises-dps-audit|witness-float64-padding-audit|witness-raw-float64-audit|q0-value-drift-audit|no-free-parameter-certificate|codata-truncation-audit|witness-value-copy-audit|compute-audit-scan|derivation-chain-audit|e0-calibration-audit)\.witness\.json$' && \ git rebase --skip # 2. If a mixed commit accidentally included a contended audit witness alongside real work, # take origin/main's copy (--ours during rebase onto origin/main) so your commit drops the diff: git checkout --ours -- <contended-audit-witness.json> git add <contended-audit-witness.json> git rebase --continue . And whenever you run scripts/compute-qa.py or scripts/precision-gates.sh locally on a feature branch, always revert any dirtied contended audit witnesses before staging (git checkout -- computations/audits/ computations/*.witness.json). For .qa.json sidecar conflicts during rebase, resolve script entries to origin/main and restore agent verdicts mechanically via: python3 scripts/qa-sidecar-agent-union.py --against <pre-rebase-ref> --apply. Only flag the user if: . | The conflict is in a source file (.py, .lean, .ts, .md) — those are real semantic conflicts that need human judgment. | The conflict is in a witness other than the three audit witnesses above (e.g. markov-trace-axiomatic-multi-atom.witness.json has a substantive numerical drift — that means a CI-run script on main produced different numerical output, which deserves a closer look before blindly accepting). | The auto-resolve recipe itself fails (regen script errors out, push rejected for non-fast-forward reasons, etc.). | . For witnesses specifically: if upstream regenerated *.witness.json files our branch also touched, prefer rebase-and-regenerate over hand-merging the JSON. Witness drift is structural; merging is fragile. Q3 — Can we reuse? . Apply the four reuse questions from prepare-merge.md §2a: . | Definitions / lemmas / simulators / witnesses — does the new commit add something our branch is duplicating, paraphrasing, or reinventing? Replace with uses[] / \cite{} and delete the local stand-in. | Proofs — does a new lemma or tactic discharge a hypothesis, collapse a calc chain, or close a sorry? Apply via local/proof-simplifier (narrative) + local/lean-build-fix / local/lean-completeness-audit (Lean). | Exposition — does our .md re-derive what main now defines upstream? Replace with a forward-reference; route through local/scientific-accuracy / local/readability-editing. | Computation — does a new script or witness in computations/ supersede a hand-rolled loop or stale witness in our branch? Swap in and regenerate the witness JSON. (See §2a for the routine compute-audit-scan / derivation- chain-audit / e0-calibration-audit drift-conflict pattern.) . | When the upstream commit adds or modifies a prop: / thm: / lem: / cor: block (or its .lean sibling), delegate to local/compute-integration-watcher to check whether the new claim is wired into the production compute chain. The watcher runs the I1–I12 wiring checklist and returns a verdict (WIRED / PROBE-ONLY / NOT-WIRED) plus a concrete fix recommendation. Capture the verdict here and feed it into Q4. | . | . Q3a — Did upstream land a new skill file? . For each main-refresh, check whether .claude/skills/local/*.md (or .claude/skills/<pkg>/*.md) gained a new file between this branch’s prior baseline and the new origin/main: . git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A "$LAST_BASE..origin/main" \ -- '.claude/skills/local/*.md' '.claude/skills/*/*.md' . For each new skill file: . | Read its frontmatter — extract name, roles, description, and any inherits field. | Match against branch scope — does the skill’s description overlap with what this branch is doing? Heuristics: . | skill description mentions a file kind / domain / pattern that appears in this branch’s git diff origin/main..HEAD --name-only, OR | skill is a new integration-watcher child (inherits: local/integration-watcher) and your branch is itself an integration-watcher PR, OR | skill is a content-block QA skill (e.g. one-voice-*, proof-*, compute-*) and your branch touches .md / .ts / .lean content blocks. | . | Surface to the user via AskUserQuestion with the standard 3-chip pattern: . New skill <name> landed on main: . <one-line description from frontmatter> . This branch’s scope overlaps because <one-line match rationale + file paths>. 1) Adopt now — invoke the skill on the relevant subset of this branch’s diff before continuing. 2) Defer to follow-up branch — record the decision and note for the next branch; don’t change this branch. 3) Not relevant — record so the watcher doesn’t re-prompt on future main-refreshes. | Record the decision in the watcher’s ledger (.beans/<watcher-name>-ledger.md for integration-watcher children, or chat-only for the bare /watch flow) so subsequent main-refreshes don’t re-prompt for the same skill. | . This rule applies to skill files only (.claude/skills/local/*.md and .claude/skills/<pkg>/*.md). Skills landing on sibling PRs that haven’t merged yet do NOT trigger this check — only main commits count, mirroring the §2 “watch origin/main” scope. Q4 — Report or act? . | Acted (made the change): one-line summary + the new commit SHA. | Will act after current task: add a TODO with what + why. | Skipped: one-line reason (“no overlap”, “blocked on $TASK”). | .

8435.title: 4.  Stop the watcher
8435.content: Stop when the branch ships (PR merged, or you switch branches): . | Branch mode: call TaskStop on the Monitor task ID. | PR mode: the harness auto-unsubscribes when the PR merges/closes; otherwise call mcp__github__unsubscribe_pr_activity. | .

8436.title: 5.  Common upstream patterns (heuristics)
8436.content: . | Witness drift: upstream regenerated *.witness.json while we also modified them → rebase-and-regenerate, never hand-merge. | Lean version bumps: a Mathlib hash changed in lakefile.toml → check cat .lake/packages/mathlib/lean-toolchain aligns with our branch’s lean-toolchain before continuing the Lean build. | Schema migrations: if folio/schema/ changed, run cd content && bun run migrate-lean-refs and bun run validate before continuing. | Routine review-cycle commits (Gemini/Copilot fixes on unrelated PRs): almost always Q1 = no overlap = skip with one-liner. | .

8437.title: 5b.  Monitor-timeout recovery (MANDATORY when re-arming)
8437.content: Background Monitors time out ([Monitor timed out — re-arm if needed]). Do not just re-arm and continue — between the last event and the timeout, main may have moved substantially. Mandatory steps on timeout-recovery: . # Compare current baseline against actual main HEAD git fetch origin main 2>/dev/null SAFE=$(echo "<BRANCH>" | tr '/' '_') LAST=$(cat /tmp/_watch_baseline_${SAFE}.sha 2>/dev/null || echo "") CUR=$(git rev-parse origin/<BRANCH>) if [ "$LAST" != "$CUR" ]; then MISSED=$(git log --oneline "$LAST..$CUR" 2>/dev/null | wc -l) echo "MISSED $MISSED commits while watcher was down" git log --oneline "$LAST..$CUR" | head -10 # Update baseline AFTER reporting git rev-parse origin/<BRANCH> > /tmp/_watch_baseline_${SAFE}.sha fi . If MISSED >= 5 OR any missed commit touches a file in your branch’s diff, run the §3 integration checklist on the missed range BEFORE arming a fresh monitor. This catches the failure mode where a focused work session (axiom discharge sweep, content authoring marathon, witness regeneration loop) silently lets main move 10+ commits ahead while the watcher is timed out.

8438.title: 6.  Output style
8438.content: Match user-accessibility note in AGENTS.md: . | One sentence per commit / event by default | Numbered choices when integration is non-obvious | Run small fixes proactively; flag big ones | .

8446.title: Web apps — an app is content, the harness publishes it
8446.content: Skill web-apps: Interactive web apps as knowledge-graph content: a layer holds an app’s source in a directory of kind web-app (one web-app.json), its UI strings go through the harness’s translation process like any template, and the harness’s apps visualiser (Tool web-app-build) builds it at publish and writes it to its own route with no site chrome, loaded only when a reader opens it. Read before adding an app to any layer, before writing a publish script for one (do not), and when an app’s build or translations fail. Named by: Publish a web app — declared, translated, built at its own route . Skill id: web-apps · Package: ui-core · Kind: web-app · Tool: web-app-build (bun run cat web-apps:build) · Process: web-app-publish .

8447.title: The rule
8447.content: A layer that carries an app declares it; it does not publish it. Owner, 2026-11-11 (cards Q-GAME-5 A and Q-GAME-7 A): a content layer with an app (a WHO onboarding game was the first) must not become a harness to ship it, and the one-off route VaxLink used (web/ + its own publish.sh + site.build.keep) is retired. The kind and its visualiser are the harness’s, so every layer that mounts cat-harness gets them. Before writing an app at all, ask whether it is a journey: a walkthrough of people and steps is a user-scenario and a workshop drawn by the journeys-viewer, not an app. An app is for what a page cannot be: a game, a simulation, a 3D world.

8448.title: Declaring one
8448.content: . | Put the app’s source in a directory of the layer, with its package.json and a lockfile (package-lock.json for npm, bun.lock for bun): the build installs exact versions only. | Declare the directory in the layer’s <name>.json with "graphTypologies": ["web-app"]. | Put a web-app.json (web-app/0.1.0, the schema the Tool web-app-build reads) at its root: | . { "$schema": "web-app/0.1.0", "id": "onboarding-game", "title": "Join the Network", "description": "A country onboards to the GDHCN, one choice at a time.", "build": { "installer": "npm", "script": "build", "outDir": "dist" }, "locales": ["en", "ar", "es", "fr", "ru", "zh"], "i18n": { "catalog": "src/i18n/en.json", "out": "public/i18n" }, "contentFrom": ["business-processes", "glossary"], "sizeBudgetMB": 45, "license": "Apache-2.0", "source": { "repository": "https://github.com/carlsbox/gdhcn-onboarding-game", "commit": "bd4c34c" } } . | field | rule | . | id | lower-case kebab; the route segment. Two layers claiming one id is a declaration error naming both. | . | build | defaults npm / build / dist. The app must build with relative asset paths (Vite base: './'), since its route is computed, not chosen. | . | chrome | always none (the default): the app draws its own frame. | . | locales | the first is the source language. A WHO layer ships the six UN languages: ar, en, es, fr, ru, zh. Arabic is right to left: the app sets dir="rtl" for it. | . | contentFrom | the layer’s own directory ids the app reads at build time. An app reads the layer’s content (its BPMN, glossary, actors, instances) at build time rather than copying it into code, so it cannot drift. | . | sizeBudgetMB | the index flags an app over it; the site size review reads it. | . | license, source | for a copied app: keep its LICENSE and a NOTICE naming the source commit. | .

8449.title: Where it is published, and why it loads only when opened
8449.content: | route | what | . | <locale>/<harness>/apps/ | the index, in the site’s chrome: one entry per app, its languages and size | . | <locale>/<harness>/apps/<id>/ | the app’s build, every page marked <meta name="folio-navbar" content="none"> and rendered-by: web-app-build | . The route is computed by visualiserRoute, as for every visualiser (harness-tiles). No other page embeds an app or loads its scripts: a tile, an IG page or a journey links to it. So a reader downloads an app only by opening its route. Inside the app, put heavy parts (a 3D engine, films) behind a dynamic import() or preload="none" so the first screen paints first. Lazy on screen, complete in print . Defer what a reader may never reach (owner, 2026-11-14: “do lazy load content and libs”): images with loading="lazy" and decoding="async", libraries behind a dynamic import() on first use, a hidden panel or a closed <details> drawn on its first open, a popout built when it is opened. Every deferral has a print path (owner, 2026-11-14: “make sure printing loads all of the content before it renders the PDF on the browser”). On beforeprint, and in a Print button that waits before it calls window.print(): switch lazy images to eager and wait for them, build and open what is built on toggle, and write out text that only a popout shows. afterprint closes again what the preparation opened. The library entry page (cat-harness-tools/scripts/lib/library-document.ts, docPrintPrep) is the worked example.

8450.title: Translating an app — the harness’s process, not a second one
8450.content: An app’s UI strings are one more template to the translation process (translation-manager, translation-refresh, multi-locale-translation.bpmn): . | Source catalog. i18n.catalog is a flat JSON object { key: text } in the source locale. Placeholders are {name}. Nothing else is translatable: no strings hard-coded in components. | Templates. bun run cat web-apps:build --extract writes translations/<locale>/apps/<id>.pot in the declaring layer, one ui-string entry per key with the key as msgctxt. Name this command in the layer’s AGENTS.md §Translations as the app’s “refresh the templates” step, so the watcher runs it. | Translation. Translators fill translations/<locale>/apps/<id>.po exactly as for pages and diagrams: one PR per locale, the fixed terms, the untainted round trip, officiality as the layer declares it. | Injection is the build. Before building, the Tool writes each locale’s translated strings to <i18n.out>/<locale>.json. The app loads its locale’s file and falls back to the source text per string. | Gates. web-apps:build --check fails on a stale template, a translation that drops or adds a {placeholder}, or a translation for a key the catalog no longer has. Untranslated strings are reported, never failed. | . Media that speaks (narration, films) is not a string: list each clip per locale in the app’s own data, and say in the app when a locale has captions only.

8453.title: Wireframe design review
8453.content: Skill wireframe-design-review: Design a user interface (a page, a visualiser, a navbar) by the WireGen methodology: a written design intent, at least two mid-fidelity HTML candidates, each with a web AND a mobile layout, mechanical checks at both viewports, a blind per-criterion review, adjudication where reviewers disagree, and a recorded choice. Also how an EXISTING visualiser is wireframed as-is, so that every declared visualiser has a wireframe with a QA sidecar. Process: processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn. Called for Design use from CRDM (Process_CRDM_Requirements, Call_Wireframe) whenever a requirement changes a rendered surface, before anything is built. Named by: Adopt a methodology from a source document, Translation Workflow, Copy a knowledge-graph asset into a folio, A sub-graph wants to leave, Authorise the extraction, Move the graph into its repositories, Prepare a graph to stand alone, A knowledge graph leaves for its own repositories, Build and publish a per-slice SQLite file, A sub-KG is staged in place, then leaves for its own repository, Adjudication, Ask the person, CRDM close-out, CRDM data model, CRDM Phase 6 — implement, MVP, acceptance, CRDM — link the work to an issue, CRDM Phase 1 — needs, CRDM Phases 2–4 — BPA and requirements, CRDM requirements, CRDM Phase 5 — beans and sign-off, Hand back to the discussion, Options analysis, Related work: find, sort, summarize, ask to coordinate, Secure agent permissions, Session state machine, SWOT situation analysis, Wireframe design review, Contributor feedback on a working draft, Record agent step, Review-log watch . Method: wiregen. Process: processes/ui/wireframe-design-review.bpmn.

8454.title: Where wireframes live
8454.content: | use | directory | . | As-is | <instance>/docs/wireframes/<topic>/, in the layer that declares the visualiser: cat-harness/docs/wireframes/<topic>/ for this harness’s own pages, and a content layer’s own docs/wireframes/<topic>/ for a page it declares | . | Design, from a CRDM request | docs/proposals/<slug>/wireframes/, beside the request’s proposal docs/proposals/<slug>.md: the candidates are assets of the proposal. When the proposal is filed (git mv to docs/requirements/, crdm-requirements-workflow (opt-in cat-harness.sdlc)), its asset directory moves with it in the same commit. | . Either directory holds: . | intent.md | one HTML file per candidate | authors.json, which reviewers are not shown | checks/: screenshots and the checker’s report | reviews/: one file per reviewer | . Each layer’s docs/wireframes/index.json maps the visualiser refs that layer declares to the wireframe that covers each. bun run cat check:wireframes reads every such index in the checkout, writes the QA sidecar (test/results/wireframes.qa-results.json) and fails on any gap. A wireframe sits with its page because an index naming another layer’s page reads as an undeclared ref wherever that layer is not mounted; another layer’s wireframes are reported as <instance>/<topic>.

8455.title: Input and output
8455.content: The contract is input.schema.json and output.schema.json. | In: the use (design or as-is), the topic (for CRDM, the proposal slug), the surface, and, from CRDM, the requirements that change it, the proposal path, the humanReviewer (requester or BA), the channels the candidates are shown in, and the branch. | Out — the renderings: assetDir, intent, and one candidates[] entry per candidate: its source HTML path, its screenshots.web and screenshots.mobile paths (from wireframe-check), their staging deep links, its per-criterion entries, and its outcome with the reason. chosen names the candidate, who chose it and the comment that records it; it is absent until a person chooses. | Out — as changed assets: changedAssets[] lists every wireframe file the branch adds, changes or removes (candidate HTML, screenshots, intent, reviews) in the record shape a staging preview’s graph carries (change, kind, title, before, after, source, pages or pagesUnknown; ChangedAsset in cat-harness-tools scripts/kg-changed-assets.ts). The review therefore lists the drawings the same way it lists every other changed asset. | Out — staging links: stagingLinks, the shape every request for feedback carries (staging-review), copied inline as definitions.stagingLinks. | .

8456.title: Two uses
8456.content: | use | candidates | review | . | Design: a new or changed UI | at least two, compared blind | per-criterion, then adjudication, then options analysis | . | As-is: an existing visualiser, drawn as it renders on main | exactly one, marked as-is | the same criteria. A finding becomes a work item against the visualiser, not a redesign | .

8457.title: 1. Intent
8457.content: A few sentences: who the screen is for, what they need to do, and what it must show. For an as-is wireframe, the intent is read off the visualiser’s own declaration and generator, not invented.

8458.title: 2. Candidates
8458.content: . | Mid-fidelity HTML: monochrome, real content from the graph it shows, semantic icons, and no placeholder text. | Web and mobile in every candidate, through responsive CSS or two layouts. A candidate with one layout does not enter review. | .

8459.title: 3. Mechanical checks (wireframe-viewport-check)
8459.content: bun run cat wireframe:check --use as-is --topic <topic> --surface <visualiser ref> bun run cat wireframe:check --use design --topic <slug> --surface <surface> . The three flags are this skill’s input. --topic picks the directory in the table above and every candidate in it (name candidates to check fewer; one outside it is refused), and the report goes to its checks/. --use design needs at least two candidates; --use as-is needs each marked as-is in its file name, and a --surface that is the topic or a ref index.json says it covers. The use, topic and surface are recorded in report.json. This renders each candidate at web (1280×800) and mobile (390×844) sizes. It records script entries for renders, no-overflow and no-placeholder, each pass or fail with a note, and writes a screenshot per viewport. Any fail sends the candidate back to step 2.

8460.title: 4. Blind review, per criterion
8460.content: Reviewers include at least one agent that did not author the candidate and one human. For Design use called from CRDM, the human is the requester or the BA who owns the request: the person who will accept the delivered feature chooses its design. They see the intent, the screenshots and the HTML, without the authors. For each criterion they record pass, warn or fail, with a reason: . | criterion | question | . | intent-fit | Does it do what the intent says, for the person it names? | . | web usability | Can the task be done at desktop width? | . | mobile usability | Can the task be done at phone width, by touch? | . | accessibility | Contrast, a non-colour channel, accessible names, keyboard, reading order | . | alternatives | Do the candidates differ in the ways that matter? (Design use only) | . There are no scores and no averages (methodology-adoption, Refusals).

8461.title: 5. Adjudication and choice
8461.content: . | When entries for one criterion disagree, call Process_Adjudication. The adjudication leads, the checker’s entry is kept, and a dispensation needs its reason. | The choice between surviving candidates is Process_OptionsAnalysis. Rejected candidates stay, each with the reason it lost. | .

8462.title: Staging links
8462.content: When a staging preview exists, every request this skill makes for feedback, review or sign-off carries it: one deep link per changed page, to the anchor where the change sits, with the same page on main as before. Where the skill declares an output contract, they go in its stagingLinks field. The rule, and where the page list comes from: feedback-deep-links.

8463.title: Showing it to the requester
8463.content: Design use from CRDM ends in a person’s choice, so the candidates must be in front of that person before implementation starts: . | Commit the candidates, intent.md, checks/ (screenshots) and reviews/ under docs/proposals/<slug>/wireframes/ on the feature branch, so feature-staging publishes them with the rest of the branch. | Show them where the requester will look, chosen from context: the conversation, the issue the request came from, the pull request, or more than one of these. Where it goes is a judgement (feedback-deep-links, point 5); every place chosen carries the same content: a short narrative of what each candidate does differently; branches/ deep links to each candidate’s HTML (not the site root); and its web and mobile screenshots shown as images, not only linked. Say which could not be linked or rendered, and why. | Ask the requester or BA to choose, with the comparison (one row per candidate, from A_CompareOptions) and a recommendation, per interaction-modality where it applies. | Record their choice in the proposal and in the output’s chosen. An agent never chooses on their behalf. Implementation (CRDM Phase 6) builds against the chosen candidate, and the delivery summary links it beside the after-screenshot. | .

8467.title: Wireframe design review
8467.content: Process_WireframeDesignReview · advisory · 6 step(s) . WireGen (methodologies/wiregen) made executable: a written design intent, at least two mid-fidelity candidates each with a web AND a mobile layout, mechanical checks, a blind per-criterion review, adjudication where reviewers disagree, and a recorded choice. A wireframe is part of the design process for adjudication. Operating skill: wireframe-design-review. The same mechanical checks back the as-is wireframe every declared visualiser owes, which check:wireframes runs. i i i i i i Actors: Designer · Feedback providers · Adjudicator .

8469.title: Lanes — who acts
8469.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Designer | authoring-agent | Writes the intent, produces candidates with real content, and runs the mechanical checks. Does not review its own candidates. | . | Feedback providers | feedback-provider | One or more reviewers (agent and human) who see candidates shuffled, without their author, and record pass, warn or fail per criterion with a reason. There are no scores and no averages. | . | Adjudicator | adjudicator | Reached only when entries for one criterion disagree. Settles the disagreement with a reason, and decides between surviving candidates through options analysis. | .

8470.title: Steps
8470.content: Every one of the 6 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | Write the design intentD_Intent | Designer | wireframe-design-review | A short statement of who the screen is for, what they need to do, and what it must show. It is the criterion every candidate is judged against. | . | Produce >= 2 candidates, web + mobileD_Candidates | Designer | wireframe-design-review | Mid-fidelity HTML: monochrome, real folio content, semantic icons, no placeholder text. Each candidate has both a web layout and a mobile layout. | . | Mechanical checks, both viewportsD_Check | Designer | wireframe-design-review | Tool wireframe-check renders every candidate at a web and a mobile viewport. It fails on horizontal overflow at mobile width, on placeholder text, and on a missing viewport, and writes screenshots and a script entry per criterion. | . | Blind review per criterionR_Review | Feedback providers | wireframe-design-review | Criteria: intent-fit, web usability, mobile usability, accessibility, and alternatives considered. A review at one viewport only is incomplete. | . | AdjudicationCall_Adjudicate | Adjudicator | calls Criterion adjudication | folio-assistant’s adjudication: the adjudication leads, the checker’s entry is kept, and the dispensation carries its reason. Reviewers disagreeing on ONE criterion is a criterion disagreement, so this calls the QA-criterion specialisation: the failing entry stands, the criterion does not apply to this screen, or a dispensation is granted with its reason.The entry condition matches exactly rather than approximately: GW_Agree asks whether the blind reviewers’ entries agree and takes no here, and Process_CriterionAdjudication starts at “entries for one criterion disagree” — R_Review records pass, warn or fail PER CRITERION with a reason, so the disagreement reaching this step is a per-criterion disagreement between reviewer entries and nothing else. | . | Choose a candidateCall_Choose | Adjudicator | calls Options analysis | A one-off choice between surviving candidates. 8473.title: Refresh computation witnesses
8473.content: Process_WitnessRefresh · strict (defaulted) · 6 step(s) . Bring qou’s computation witnesses back in line with the producers that write them, without a witness ever being rewritten that the owner did not approve. Owner, 2026-10-04: “all witnesses tools will need to go into the KG”; this is the process those Tools run in. A WITNESS IS CONTENT HERE. Its numbers are what the paper quotes, so the owner’s rule that a migration changes no mathematics applies to it, and so does the ask-first rule for refreshing one. That is why the decision sits in the owner’s lane between the measurement and the re-run, and why nothing before it writes a file: the dry run and the parity check both work on the committed tree or a scratch copy of it. THE PLAN IS run_pipeline.py --dry-run --content-only, UNCHANGED. The process does not re-derive staleness; it calls the pipeline’s own answer through the witness-refresh-plan Tool, so the list a person approves is exactly the list the pipeline would act on. No rendered diagram — run bun run cat render:bpmn.

8475.title: Lanes — who acts
8475.content: | lane | role | what it does here | . | Owner (the paper’s author) | — | Decides which stale witnesses may be rewritten. A witness whose re-run changes a number, rather than only provenance fields, needs a judgement about which result is right; that judgement is not the agent’s. | . | Compute agent | — | Measures before anyone decides, and acts only on what was approved. Writes nothing to the tree until the owner’s lane says which producers to re-run. | .

8476.title: Steps
8476.content: Every one of the 6 step(s) is documented. | step | lane | skill / sub-process | what it does | . | List stale producers (pipeline dry run)Task_Plan | Compute agent | — | Run python3 computations/run_pipeline.py --dry-run --content-only (the witness-refresh-plan Tool). It lists every content-linked producer whose witness is stale (script changed, a dependency changed, or a stale q0) in dependency order, and writes nothing. | . | Classify each: does a re-run reproduce it?Task_Parity | Compute agent | — | Run the platform’s witness-parity Tool on the listed witnesses. It re-runs each committed producer in a scratch git worktree and reports pass, fail (with the differing paths) or unknown (environment mismatch, stale script, error, timeout). The owner sees, for each candidate, whether a refresh would change numbers or only provenance. | . | Approve which producers to re-runTask_Approve | Owner (the paper’s author) | — | The owner picks the producers whose witnesses may be rewritten, from the classified list. Saying nothing approves none. A witness whose re-run changes numbers needs a decision about which result is right before it is approved. | . | Re-run the approved producersTask_Run | Compute agent | — | Re-run exactly the approved producers, in dependency order. A producer that writes sibling witnesses outside the approved set is reported, and those files are restored to their committed state rather than committed. | . | Precision gates; keep audit output outTask_Gates | Compute agent | — | Run scripts/precision-gates.sh --changed. A red that names one of the refreshed witnesses stops the process at the producer. A red that predates the change does not, but it is reported. The gate scripts rewrite their own audit-report witnesses as a side effect; those are restored, never committed. | . | Commit the refreshed witnessesTask_Commit | Compute agent | — | Commit only the approved witnesses, naming the producers, the fields that changed and the gate result, and re-run witness-parity on them, expecting pass. | .

8479.title: State in a running process
8479.content: Skill workflow-state: Where a running process keeps what it knows, and which store answers which question. The three records a step may touch, the one it may not, what <cat-harness.processes:bean op> actually performs, and why an instance and a work item must be one answer rather than two. Named by: Adopt a methodology from a source document, Translation Workflow, Copy a knowledge-graph asset into a folio, A sub-graph wants to leave, Authorise the extraction, Move the graph into its repositories, Prepare a graph to stand alone, A knowledge graph leaves for its own repositories, Build and publish a per-slice SQLite file, A sub-KG is staged in place, then leaves for its own repository, Ask the person, CRDM close-out, CRDM data model, CRDM Phase 6 — implement, MVP, acceptance, CRDM — link the work to an issue, CRDM Phase 1 — needs, CRDM Phases 2–4 — BPA and requirements, CRDM requirements, CRDM Phase 5 — beans and sign-off, Hand back to the discussion, Related work: find, sort, summarize, ask to coordinate, Secure agent permissions, Session state machine, Wireframe design review, Contributor feedback on a working draft, Record agent step, Review-log watch . A process instance is not self-contained. It walks a diagram that lives somewhere else, records its position somewhere else again, and reads facts it must not change. Five stores; confusing any two of them is how a work plan comes to disagree with itself.

8480.title: Which store answers which question
8480.content: | question | store | graph typology | layer | . | what does this process DO? | processes/**/*.bpmn | cat-harness | content | . | where did this instance GET TO? | the workflow-state node of the work item graph | workflow-state | state | . | what is being worked on? | the bean-defs node of the work item graph | bean-defs | state | . | what does a PERSON still owe? | todos/ | todo-items | state | . | what do I already know? | agent memory | memory | context | . The layer column says what a step may do. A step may write to a state graph; that is what state is for. A step that writes to context is a defect, not an update: memory changes when a human directs an authoring act, outside any instance. content-context-and-state-graphs carries the axis; processMayWrite() is the predicate.

8481.title: The diagram is content and the instance is state, and that is the whole model
8481.content: A .bpmn is authored, reviewed, versioned and read by anyone — it stands on its own. An instance is a token position in that diagram plus a history: it means nothing detached from the file it walks. That is why the two live in different graphs and why an instance names its process rather than embedding it. Two consequences: . An instance is never edited by hand. It carries "$schema": "folio-workflow-instance/v1" and the interpreter owns it. Hand- editing a token is asserting a step happened, which is precisely what the gate exists to refuse. A diagram change does not rewrite history. An instance records where it got to under the diagram as it stood. If a step is renamed, the honest answer is that the old instance names a node that no longer exists — not that it retroactively took a different path.

8482.title: Beans and instances are ONE answer, not two
8482.content: bean-defs says what is being worked on; workflow-state says where it got to. Those must be one answer or they diverge, and a work plan that disagrees with itself is worse than one that is merely coarse. The loop is closed by <cat-harness.processes:bean op="…"> on an activity. A bean-marked step is not a step about the work plan — it IS the work-plan operation, so completing the step performs it: . | op | on completing the step | . | claim | status → in-progress, idempotent | . | note | append the caller’s note to the body | . | resolve | status → completed, only if the instance itself finished (or only archive steps are left) | . | archive | move a completed or scrapped work item into the archive, only once the instance finished | . claim is drawn only in Process_BeanOpen, and resolve and archive only in Process_BeanClose; every process that works on a work item calls both (check:bean-calls). note is drawn where the work happens. resolve is the careful one. A work item is never closed on somebody else’s judgement, so it does not fire on the caller’s say-so: the work item completes only when the instance tracking it has completed, which is a fact derived from the process rather than asserted by the agent calling it. A still-running instance gets a note. An op the build does not implement fails at process load. A step that says it resolves a work item and quietly does nothing is exactly the divergence the extension exists to close.

8483.title: What state does NOT buy you
8483.content: Ordering is not quality. A completed instance means the gates ran in order and a person saw the findings. Whether the content is correct is what the QA axes, the build and the validators are for. A green process must never be read as a reviewed artefact, and any dashboard built on this has to say so. A position is not a claim. An instance at Task_Commit says the token arrived, not that the commit is good.

8484.title: Where running instances live — the state graph on the branch store
8484.content: Running instances are part of the work-plan store (workflow-state graph typology; positions in work-plan-store (opt-in cat-harness.work-plan)). Where the deployment uses the git state-branch Tool, the store is mounted and pushed as described in work-plan-store-git-branch. The container is ephemeral and a work plan only one agent can see is not a work plan. Instance state lives in the shared work-plan store for the same reason work item definitions do: a sibling session, or the same session resumed in a fresh container, reads the store to find the position that exists rather than starting a second one beside it. When an instance advances, its state is written through the store’s Tool (bun run cat state:push when backed by the git state branch). This keeps instance state globally visible without cluttering code PR diffs on main. Instance ids are derived from the subject rather than random, so re-entering a step finds the instance that is already there: beans create is not idempotent and dedupes on nothing, so an id you can recompute is what prevents duplicates.

8485.title: Reading the state you did not write
8485.content: Before acting on an instance you did not start, ask what it is waiting on. A work item’s status defaults to non-blocking; a real block carries what it waits on, since when, an expiry and a handoff — because a block with no expiry cannot be told from abandoned work. bean-blocking carries that, and bean-coordination carries the rule that a claim announces rather than reserves until your PR exists.

8486.content: . | bpmn-processes — how to author an activity, strict vs advisory, the commit-boundary gate, DMN-backed gateways. | process-state — saying which process you are in, the five detectors for being out of process, and the recovery. | content-context-and-state-graphs — the layer each store sits on, and why memory is not writable by a step. | todo-manager — the work plan’s own store. A todo is a person’s outstanding item and is not a second work plan. | .
